rows.title: Python Libraries Part 1
rows.description: Master Python's built-in data structures and utilities: `list`, `tuple`, `set`, `dict`, list comprehensions, slicing, `enumerate()`, `zip()`, and the `sorted()` function with custom key lambdas.
rows.outputFormat: Demonstrate Pythonic manipulation.

examples.explanation: Python uses Timsort running in O(N log N) time.

examples.input: d = {x: x**2 for x in range(3)}

rows.title: Basic Arrays
rows.description: Comprehensive review of foundational 1D array operations, frequency hash tables, and string manipulations: linear scans, in-place element swapping, character counting, and boundary checks.
rows.outputFormat: Demonstrate linear search and frequency mapping.

rows.title: Sum of Array Elements
rows.description: Given an array of integers `nums`, calculate and return the sum of all elements in the array. Solve in O(N) time with O(1) space.
rows.outputFormat: Return the sum as an integer.

rows.title: Check for Perfect Number
rows.description: A perfect number is a positive integer that is equal to the sum of its positive proper divisors, excluding the number itself. Given an integer `n`, return `true` if `n` is a perfect number, otherwise return `false`. Solve in O(sqrt(N)) time.
rows.outputFormat: Return boolean `true` if perfect number, else `false`.

rows.title: Reverse a number
rows.description: Given a signed 32-bit integer `x`, return `x` with its digits reversed. If reversing `x` causes the value to go outside the signed 32-bit integer range `[-2^31, 2^31 - 1]`, then return 0.
rows.outputFormat: Return the reversed integer, or 0 if overflow occurs.

rows.title: Rotate String
rows.description: Given two strings `s` and `goal`, return `true` if and only if `s` can become `goal` after some number of shifts on `s`. A shift on `s` consists of moving the leftmost character of `s` to the rightmost position. Check if `s.length == goal.length` and `goal` is a substring of `(s + s)`.
rows.outputFormat: Return boolean `true` if `s` can rotate into `goal`, else `false`.
rows.constraints:
1 <= s.length, goal.length <= 100
s and goal consist of lowercase English letters.

rows.title: Sort Characters by Frequency
rows.description: Given a string `s`, sort it in decreasing order based on the frequency of the characters. The frequency of a character is the number of times it appears in the string. Return the sorted string. If there are multiple answers, return any of them.
rows.outputFormat: Return the frequency-sorted string.
rows.constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 5 * 10^5
s consists of uppercase and lowercase English letters and digits.

examples.explanation: 'e' appears twice, 'r' and 't' appear once. "eetr" is also valid.
Both 'c' and 'a' appear three times. "cccaaa" is also valid.

rows.title: Sum of First N Numbers
rows.description: Given an integer `n`, calculate the sum of the first `n` natural numbers (`1 + 2 + ... + n`) using recursion.
rows.outputFormat: Return the sum as a long integer.

rows.title: Java Collections
rows.description: Master the Java Collections Framework (JCF): `List` (`ArrayList`, `LinkedList`), `Set` (`HashSet`, `TreeSet`, `LinkedHashSet`), `Map` (`HashMap`, `TreeMap`, `LinkedHashMap`), and `Queue` (`PriorityQueue`, `ArrayDeque`). Learn `Comparable` vs. `Comparator` for custom sorting.
rows.inputFormat: An array of strings or integers.
rows.outputFormat: Demonstrate Java collection storage, retrieval, and sorting.

examples.input: Map<String, Integer> map = new HashMap<>(); map.put("apple", 3);
examples.explanation: HashMap provides O(1) average get and put operations.

examples.input: PriorityQueue<Integer> pq = new PriorityQueue<>(); pq.add(5); pq.add(1);
examples.explanation: Java PriorityQueue is a Min-Heap by default.

rows.title: Sum of Digits in a Given Number
rows.description: Given an integer `n`, compute the sum of its digits recursively: `digitSum(n) = (n % 10) + digitSum(n / 10)` with base case `digitSum(0) = 0`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the sum of digits as an integer.

rows.title: Pattern 22
rows.description: Given an integer `N`, print the Pattern 22 shape containing a concentric square spiral of numbers counting down from N to 1.
rows.inputFormat: A single positive integer `N` representing the dimension / height of the pattern.
rows.outputFormat: Print the corresponding pattern to standard output.

rows.title: Check if the Array is Sorted I
rows.description: Given an array `nums`, return `true` if the array was originally sorted in non-decreasing order, then rotated some number of positions (including zero). Otherwise, return `false`. The condition is equivalent to checking that `nums[i] > nums[(i + 1) % n]` at most once.
rows.outputFormat: Return boolean `true` if sorted and rotated, else `false`.

examples.explanation: Cannot be obtained by rotation of sorted array.

rows.title: Second Highest Occurring Element
rows.description: Given an array of integers `nums`, find the element that appears with the second highest frequency. If multiple elements tie, return the smallest element. If fewer than 2 distinct frequencies exist, return -1.
rows.outputFormat: Return the second highest occurring element, or -1.

examples.explanation: Highest frequency is 3 (element 1), second highest is 2 (element 2).

rows.title: Find missing number
rows.description: Given an array `nums` containing `n` distinct numbers in the range `[0, n]`, return the only number in the range that is missing from the array. Solve in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space (using sum formula or bitwise XOR).
rows.inputFormat: An integer array `nums` of length `n` containing distinct numbers in range `[0, n]`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the single integer from `[0, n]` missing from `nums`.
rows.constraints:
n == nums.length
1 <= n <= 10^5
0 <= nums[i] <= n
All the numbers of nums are unique.

examples.explanation: n = 3 since there are 3 numbers, so all numbers are in the range [0,3]. 2 is the missing number in the range since it does not appear in nums.
n = 2 since there are 2 numbers, so all numbers are in the range [0,2]. 2 is missing.

rows.title: Basic String
rows.description: Understand string representations in memory: character arrays, ASCII encoding (e.g. `'a'` is 97, `'A'` is 65), immutability (in Java/Python), and string concatenation performance (`StringBuilder` vs. string addition).
rows.outputFormat: Demonstrate basic string indexing, length, and ASCII translation.

rows.title: Divisors of a Number
rows.description: Given an integer `n`, find all of its positive divisors and return them in sorted order. Solve in O(sqrt(N)) time by iterating up to sqrt(n) and adding both `i` and `n / i`.
rows.outputFormat: Return a sorted list of all positive divisors.

rows.title: Sum of Highest and Lowest Frequency
rows.description: Given an array of integers `nums`, find the maximum frequency of any element and the minimum frequency of any element in the array. Return the sum of the highest and lowest frequencies.
rows.outputFormat: Return an integer representing (maxFreq + minFreq).

examples.explanation: Max frequency is 3 (for element 3), min frequency is 1 (for element 1). Sum = 3 + 1 = 4.

rows.title: Isomorphic Strings
rows.description: Given two strings `s` and `t`, determine if they are isomorphic. Two strings `s` and `t` are isomorphic if the characters in `s` can be replaced to get `t`. All occurrences of a character must be replaced with another character while preserving the order of characters. No two characters may map to the same character, but a character may map to itself.
rows.outputFormat: Return boolean `true` if isomorphic, else `false`.
rows.constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 5 * 10^4
t.length == s.length
s and t consist of any valid ASCII character.

rows.title: Check if String is Palindrome or Not
rows.description: Given a string `s`, determine if it is a palindrome using recursion. Compare `s[i]` with `s[n - 1 - i]` and recurse on `i + 1` until the midpoint is reached.
rows.outputFormat: Return boolean `true` if palindrome, else `false`.

rows.title: Left Rotate Array by K Places
rows.description: Given an integer array `nums`, rotate the array to the left by `k` steps, where `k` is non-negative. Implement this in-place using O(1) extra memory (e.g. reversal algorithm).
rows.inputFormat: An integer array `nums` of length `n` and a non-negative integer `k`.
rows.outputFormat: Return or modify in-place the array after rotating left by `k` positions.

examples.explanation: Rotate left 1 step: [2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 1]. Rotate 2 steps: [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 1, 2]. Rotate 3 steps: [4, 5, 6, 7, 1, 2, 3].
After rotating left by 2 positions, the array becomes [3, 99, -1, -100].

rows.title: Check if the Array is Sorted II
rows.description: Given an array of integers `nums`, check if the array is sorted in non-decreasing order using recursion. Verify that `nums[i] <= nums[i + 1]` and recursively check for index `i + 1`.
rows.outputFormat: Return boolean `true` if sorted, else `false`.

examples.explanation: Array is sorted in ascending order.

rows.title: Leaders in an Array
rows.description: Given an integer array `nums`, find all the leaders in the array. An element is considered a leader if it is strictly greater than all elements to its right. The rightmost element is always a leader. Return the leaders in the order they appear from left to right.
rows.outputFormat: Return a list of leaders in the array.

examples.explanation: 17 is greater than all elements to its right [4, 3, 5, 2]. 5 is greater than [2]. 2 is the rightmost element.
4 is greater than 0, and 0 is the rightmost element.

rows.title: Intersection of two sorted arrays
rows.description: Given two sorted integer arrays `a` and `b`, find the intersection of the two arrays. Each element in the result must appear as many times as it shows in both arrays, and the result should be sorted.
rows.outputFormat: Return an array representing the intersection of `a` and `b`.

examples.explanation: Elements 2 appears twice in both, and 4 appears once in both.
No common elements between the two arrays.

rows.title: Union of two sorted arrays
rows.description: Given two sorted arrays `a` and `b`, find the union of the two arrays. The union contains all distinct elements from both arrays in sorted order.
rows.inputFormat: Two sorted integer arrays `a` of length `n` and `b` of length `m`.
rows.outputFormat: Return a sorted list of unique integers appearing in either `a` or `b`.

examples.explanation: Distinct elements including both arrays in sorted order are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7.
The union of both arrays without duplicate entries is [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].

rows.title: Reverse Pairs
rows.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return the number of reverse pairs in the array. A reverse pair is a pair `(i, j)` where `0 <= i < j < nums.length` and `nums[i] > 2 * nums[j]`. Solve in O(N log N) time using modified Merge Sort count.
rows.outputFormat: Return the total count of reverse pairs as an integer.

examples.explanation: The two reverse pairs are (1, 4) since nums[1] = 3 > 2*1, and (3, 4) since nums[3] = 3 > 2*1.

rows.title: Count Inversions
rows.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return the number of inversions in the array. Two elements `nums[i]` and `nums[j]` form an inversion if `nums[i] > nums[j]` and `i < j`. Solve in O(N log N) time using modified Merge Sort.
rows.outputFormat: Return the total number of inversions as a long integer.

examples.explanation: Every pair forms an inversion in a reverse sorted array. Total = 5*4/2 = 10.

rows.title: Find the repeating and missing number
rows.description: You are given a read-only array of `n` integers with values between `1` and `n`. Each integer appears exactly once, except `A` which appears twice and `B` which is missing. Return `[A, B]` representing the repeating and missing numbers. Solve in O(N) time and O(1) extra space using mathematics or XOR.
rows.inputFormat: An integer array `nums` of length `n` containing numbers from `1` to `n`.
rows.outputFormat: Return a pair/array `[repeating, missing]`.

examples.explanation: 3 repeats twice and 4 is missing from range [1, 5].
3 is repeated and 2 is missing from range [1, 3].

rows.title: Next Permutation
rows.description: A permutation of an array of integers is an arrangement of its members into a sequence or linear order. Find the next lexicographically greater permutation of its numbers. If no such arrangement is possible (it is the largest possible permutation), rearrange it as the lowest possible order (sorted in ascending order). The replacement must be in-place using O(1) extra memory.
rows.outputFormat: Rearrange `nums` into its lexicographical next permutation in-place.

examples.explanation: The next lexicographical arrangement after 123 is 132.
321 is the highest permutation, so it wraps around to the lowest [1, 2, 3].

rows.title: 4 Sum
rows.description: Given an array `nums` of `n` integers, return an array of all the unique quadruplets `[nums[a], nums[b], nums[c], nums[d]]` such that `a`, `b`, `c`, and `d` are distinct indices and `nums[a] + nums[b] + nums[c] + nums[d] == target`. The solution set must not contain duplicate quadruplets.
rows.inputFormat: An integer array `nums` of length `n` and an integer `target`.
rows.outputFormat: Return a list of unique quadruplets summing to target.

examples.explanation: Three unique quadruplets sum up to 0.
Only one unique quadruplet can be formed.

rows.title: Majority Element-II
rows.description: Given an integer array of size `n`, find all elements that appear more than `⌊ n/3 ⌋` times. Solve this in O(N) time and O(1) space using extended Boyer-Moore Voting Algorithm. Note that at most two such elements can exist.
rows.outputFormat: Return a list of integers appearing more than n/3 times.

examples.explanation: 3 appears 2 times, which is strictly greater than 3/3 = 1.
Both 1 and 2 appear 1 time, which is strictly greater than 2/3 = 0.67.

rows.title: 3 Sum
rows.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all the triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j`, `i != k`, and `j != k`, and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. Notice that the solution set must not contain duplicate triplets. Solve in O(N^2) time using sorting and two pointers.
rows.outputFormat: Return a list of all unique triplets that sum to 0.

examples.explanation: The distinct triplets that sum to 0 are [-1, 0, 1] and [-1, -1, 2].
The only possible triplet does not sum up to 0.

rows.title: Set Matrix Zeroes
rows.description: Given an `m x n` integer matrix `matrix`, if an element is `0`, set its entire row and column to `0`'s. You must do it in-place using O(1) extra auxiliary space by utilizing the first row and column as state markers.
rows.outputFormat: Modify the matrix in-place such that corresponding rows and columns are zeroed.
rows.constraints:
m == matrix.length
n == matrix[0].length
1 <= m, n <= 200
-2^31 <= matrix[i][j] <= 2^31 - 1

examples.explanation: Element at (1, 1) is 0, so entire row 1 and column 1 are zeroed.
Zeros at (0, 0) and (0, 3) cause row 0, col 0, and col 3 to be zeroed.

rows.title: Sort an array of 0's 1's and 2's
rows.description: Given an array `nums` with `n` objects colored red, white, or blue, sort them in-place so that objects of the same color are adjacent, with the colors in the order red, white, and blue (represented as 0, 1, and 2 respectively). You must solve this in O(N) time with O(1) extra space using the Dutch National Flag algorithm.
rows.inputFormat: An integer array `nums` containing only values 0, 1, and 2.
rows.outputFormat: Sort the array in-place in non-decreasing order.
rows.constraints:
n == nums.length
1 <= n <= 300
nums[i] is either 0, 1, or 2.

examples.explanation: The array is partitioned into 0s first, 1s next, and 2s last.

rows.title: Search in rotated sorted array-I
rows.description: There is an integer array `nums` sorted in ascending order with distinct values. Given the array `nums` after the possible rotation and an integer `target`, return the index of `target` if it is in `nums`, or -1 if it is not in `nums`. You must write an algorithm with O(log n) runtime complexity.
rows.inputFormat: An integer array `nums` rotated at an unknown pivot, and integer `target`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the index of `target`, or -1.
rows.constraints:
1 <= nums.length <= 5000
-10^4 <= nums[i], target <= 10^4
All values of nums are unique.

examples.explanation: 3 does not exist in the array.

rows.title: Search insert position
rows.description: Given a sorted array of distinct integers `nums` and a target value `target`, return the index if the target is found. If not, return the index where it would be if it were inserted in order. You must write an algorithm with O(log n) runtime complexity.
rows.inputFormat: A sorted distinct integer array `nums` and an integer `target`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the insertion position index.
rows.constraints:
1 <= nums.length <= 10^4
-10^4 <= nums[i], target <= 10^4
nums contains distinct values sorted in ascending order.

rows.title: Find Nth root of a number
rows.description: Given two numbers `n` and `m`, find the `n`-th integer root of `m` (i.e., an integer `r` such that `r^n == m`). If no such integer root exists, return -1. Solve in O(n * log m) time using binary search on the answer range `[1, m]`.
rows.outputFormat: Return integer `r` such that `r^n == m`, or -1 if no exact integer root exists.

examples.explanation: There is no integer r such that r^4 = 69.

rows.title: Single element in sorted array
rows.description: You are given a sorted array consisting of only integers where every element appears exactly twice, except for one element which appears exactly once. Return the single element that appears only once. Your solution must run in O(log n) time and O(1) space.
rows.inputFormat: A sorted integer array `nums` where all elements appear twice except one.
rows.outputFormat: Return the single non-duplicate integer element.

examples.explanation: 2 appears only once while all other numbers appear twice.

rows.title: Find the smallest divisor
rows.description: Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `threshold`, we will choose a positive integer `divisor`, divide all the array by it, and sum the division's result. Find the smallest `divisor` such that the result mentioned above is less than or equal to `threshold`. Each result of division is rounded up to the nearest integer. Solve in O(N log(max(nums))) time using binary search on answers.
rows.inputFormat: An integer array `nums` and an integer `threshold`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the minimum positive integer divisor.

examples.explanation: If divisor is 5: ceil(1/5) + ceil(2/5) + ceil(5/5) + ceil(9/5) = 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 5 <= 6. Divisor 4 gives 7 > 6.

rows.title: Floor and Ceil in Sorted Array
rows.description: Given a sorted array `nums` and an integer `x`, find the Floor and Ceiling of `x` in `nums`. The floor of `x` is the largest element in the array smaller than or equal to `x` (`nums[i] <= x`). The ceiling of `x` is the smallest element in the array greater than or equal to `x` (`nums[i] >= x`). If floor or ceil does not exist, return -1 for that value. Return `[floor, ceil]`.
rows.inputFormat: A sorted integer array `nums` and an integer `x`.
rows.outputFormat: Return an array of two integers `[floor, ceil]`.

examples.explanation: Largest element <= 5 is 4; smallest element >= 5 is 7.
No element <= 2 exists, so floor is -1. Ceil is 3.

rows.title: Kth element of 2 sorted arrays
rows.description: Given two sorted arrays `arr1` and `arr2` of sizes `m` and `n` respectively, and an integer `k`, find the element that would be at the `k`-th position in the final combined sorted array. Solve in O(log(min(m, n))) time using binary search partitioning.
rows.inputFormat: Two sorted integer arrays `arr1`, `arr2` and an integer `k` (1-indexed).
rows.outputFormat: Return the `k`-th element of the merged sorted sequence.
rows.constraints:
1 <= arr1.length, arr2.length <= 10^5
1 <= k <= arr1.length + arr2.length
-10^9 <= arr1[i], arr2[j] <= 10^9

examples.explanation: The merged sorted array is [1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10]. The 5th element is 6.
The 7th element in the sorted combined sequence is 256.

rows.title: Learn All Patterns of Subsequences (Theory)
rows.description: Master the fundamental backtracking pattern of subsequences: the Take / Not Take recursive tree. Understand how each element either participates in the current candidate set or is excluded, yielding 2^N total branches. Learn how to format base conditions, accumulate running sums, and pass state efficiently.
rows.inputFormat: An integer array `arr` and conceptual target `k`.
rows.outputFormat: Return all subsequences generated through the standard Take/Not-Take recursive tree.

examples.explanation: All 2^3 = 8 subsequences generated in systematic order.

rows.title: Expression Add Operators
rows.description: Given a string `num` that contains only digits and an integer `target`, return all possibilities to insert the binary operators `'+'`, `'-'`, and/or `'*'` between the digits of `num` so that the resultant expression evaluates to the `target` value. Operands must not contain leading zeros.
rows.inputFormat: A string `num` of digits and integer `target`.
rows.outputFormat: Return a list of all valid expression strings.
rows.constraints:
1 <= num.length <= 10
num consists of only digits.
-2^31 <= target <= 2^31 - 1

nums[i] != nums[i + 1] for all valid i.

rows.title: Maximum Product Subarray in an Array

The product of any prefix or suffix fits in a 32-bit integer.

rows.description: Write a function that takes the binary representation of a positive integer `n` and returns the number of set bits (1s) it has (also known as the Hamming weight). Solve in O(number of set bits) time using Brian Kernighan's algorithm `n = n & (n - 1)`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the number of set bits (1s).

examples.explanation: 11 in binary is 1011, which has 3 set bits.
128 in binary is 10000000, having 1 set bit.

rows.title: Divide two numbers without multiplication and division
rows.description: Given two integers `dividend` and `divisor`, divide two integers without using multiplication, division, and mod operator. The integer division should truncate toward zero. Return the quotient after dividing dividend by divisor clamped within `[-2^31, 2^31 - 1]`. Solve in O(log^2 N) time using bit shifting.
rows.outputFormat: Return the truncated integer quotient.

rows.title: Theory
rows.description: Master the Sliding Window and Two Pointer techniques. Understand constant-size windows (fixed size `k`), dynamic-size windows (expanding right pointer and shrinking left pointer under condition violations), and prefix counting techniques `count(k) = atMost(k) - atMost(k - 1)`. These patterns reduce brute-force O(N^2) searches to linear O(N) time.
rows.inputFormat: An array `nums` of length `n` and window parameter `k`.
rows.outputFormat: Return or demonstrate window expansion and contraction logic.

examples.explanation: Max sum subarray of fixed size 3 is [5, 1, 3] with sum 9.

rows.title: Postfix to Infix Conversion
rows.description: Given a Postfix expression `s`, convert it into an Infix expression. Read the expression from left to right, pushing operands to the stack and creating `"(" + op1 + operator + op2 + ")"` on encountering operators.
rows.outputFormat: Return the infix string with parenthesis.

rows.title: Right/Left View of BT
rows.description: Given the `root` of a binary tree, return the right-side view of the binary tree (nodes visible when looked at from the right side) and the left-side view (nodes visible from left side). Solve in O(N) using recursive DFS taking the first node encountered at each level.
rows.outputFormat: Return a list of node values for the right view (or left view).
rows.constraints:
The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 100].
-100 <= Node.val <= 100

examples.explanation: From the right side, nodes 1, 3, and 4 are visible.

rows.title: Floor and Ceil in a BST
rows.description: Given a Binary Search Tree and a target `key`, find the Floor and Ceil of `key` in the BST. Floor is the greatest value <= key. Ceil is the smallest value >= key. If not present, return -1. Solve in O(height) time without inspecting the whole tree.
rows.inputFormat: The `root` of a BST and integer `key`.
rows.outputFormat: Return `[floor, ceil]`.

examples.explanation: Largest node <= 11 is 10; smallest node >= 11 is 12.
Exact key matches both floor and ceil.

rows.title: Subsets I
rows.description: Given an array of integers `nums`, return all possible subset sums in non-decreasing order. A subset sum is the sum of all elements in a particular subset.
rows.outputFormat: Return a sorted list containing the sums of all 2^n subsets.

rows.title: Sudoku Solver
rows.description: Write a program to solve a Sudoku puzzle by filling the empty cells. A sudoku solution must satisfy: 1. Each digit 1-9 must occur exactly once in each row. 2. Each digit 1-9 must occur exactly once in each column. 3. Each digit 1-9 must occur exactly once in each of the 9 `3x3` sub-boxes. Character `'.'` indicates an empty cell.
rows.outputFormat: Modify the `9x9` board in-place with the completed valid Sudoku solution.
rows.constraints:
board.length == 9
board[i].length == 9
board[i][j] is a digit '1'-'9' or '.'.
It is guaranteed that the input board has only one unique solution.

examples.explanation: All rows, columns, and 3x3 subgrids contain numbers 1-9 uniquely.

rows.title: Reverse a Doubly Linked List
rows.description: Given the `head` of a doubly linked list, reverse the list in-place and return the new head. For every node, swap its `prev` and `next` pointers in O(N) time with O(1) auxiliary space.
rows.inputFormat: The `head` of a doubly linked list.
rows.outputFormat: Return the head of the reversed doubly linked list.

examples.explanation: All prev and next pointers swapped.

rows.title: Length of loop in LL
rows.description: Given a linked list of size `n`, find the length of loop (number of nodes in the cycle) present in the list. If no loop is present, return 0. After detecting cycle collision with Floyd's algorithm, keep one pointer stationary and advance the other counting steps until it returns to the collision point.
rows.outputFormat: Return the length of the cycle, or 0.

rows.title: Check if a Number is Odd or Not
rows.description: Given a positive integer `n`, check whether `n` is odd or even using bitwise operations without using the modulo operator `%`. Note that `(n & 1) == 1` for odd numbers and `0` for even numbers.
rows.outputFormat: Return boolean `true` if odd, else `false`.

rows.title: Single Number - III
rows.description: Given an integer array `nums`, in which exactly two elements appear only once and all the other elements appear exactly twice. Find the two elements that appear only once. You can return the answer in any order. Solve in O(N) time and O(1) extra space using XOR partitioning based on the rightmost set bit.
rows.outputFormat: Return a list of two integers appearing only once.
rows.constraints:
2 <= nums.length <= 3 * 10^4
-2^31 <= nums[i] <= 2^31 - 1
Exactly two elements appear once.

rows.title: Maximum Points You Can Obtain from Cards
rows.description: There are several cards arranged in a row, and each card has an associated number of points. In one step, you can take one card from the beginning or from the end of the row. You have to take exactly `k` cards. Your score is the sum of the points of the cards you have taken. Return the maximum score you can obtain. Note: taking `k` cards from ends is equivalent to finding a contiguous subarray of length `n - k` with minimum sum.
rows.outputFormat: Return the maximum score achievable.

examples.explanation: Take three cards from the right: 5 + 6 + 1 = 12.
Score is 4 regardless of which two cards are taken.

rows.title: Implement Stack using Queue
rows.description: Implement a last-in-first-out (LIFO) stack using only a standard FIFO queue. Support `push(x)`, `pop()`, `top()`, and `empty()`. You can achieve this by rotating the single queue on each push by `size - 1` steps.

rows.outputFormat: Return results matching LIFO behavior.
rows.constraints:
1 <= x <= 9
At most 100 calls will be made to push, pop, top, and empty.

examples.explanation: Top returns 2; pop returns 2; stack is not empty.
Single item pushed and popped leaves empty stack.

rows.title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
rows.description: Given a string containing digits from `2-9` inclusive, return all possible letter combinations that the number could represent based on classic telephone keypad buttons. Return the answer in any order.
rows.outputFormat: Return a list of strings representing all combinations.
rows.constraints:
0 <= digits.length <= 4
digits[i] is a digit in the range ['2', '9'].

rows.title: Insertion before the value X in Linked List
rows.description: Given the `head` of a linked list, an integer `val`, and an existing target value `x`, insert a new node with value `val` immediately before the first node that contains value `x`.
rows.inputFormat: The `head` of a linked list, integer `val`, and integer `x`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the head of the modified list.

rows.title: Insert node before head in Doubly Linked List
rows.description: Given the `head` of a doubly linked list and an integer `val`, insert a new node with value `val` before the head in O(1) time and return the new head.
rows.inputFormat: The `head` of a DLL and integer `val`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the new head of the DLL.

rows.title: Find the starting point in LL
rows.description: Given the `head` of a linked list, return the node where the cycle begins. If there is no cycle, return `null`. Solve in O(N) time and O(1) space: after `slow` and `fast` meet, reset `slow` to `head` and advance both one step at a time until they collide at the loop starting node.
rows.outputFormat: Return the starting node of the cycle, or null.
rows.constraints:
The number of the nodes in the list is in the range [0, 10^4].
-10^5 <= Node.val <= 10^5

examples.explanation: Cycle begins at node with value 2.
Cycle begins at node with value 1.

rows.title: Clone a LL with random and next pointer
rows.description: A linked list of length `n` is given such that each node contains an additional random pointer, which could point to any node in the list, or `null`. Construct a deep copy of the list. Solve in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space by weaving clone nodes next to original nodes.
rows.inputFormat: The `head` of a linked list with random pointers.
rows.outputFormat: Return the head of the cloned linked list.
rows.constraints:
0 <= n <= 1000
-10^4 <= Node.val <= 10^4
Node.random is null or points to some node in the linked list.

examples.explanation: Deep copy reproduces node values and internal next/random pointer graph identically.

rows.title: XOR of numbers in a given range
rows.description: Given two integers `L` and `R`, find the XOR of all integers in the range `[L, R]` inclusive (`L ^ (L + 1) ^ ... ^ R`). Solve in O(1) time using the pattern of prefix XOR `1 ^ 2 ^ ... ^ N` which repeats with period 4.
rows.inputFormat: Two positive integers `L` and `R` where `L <= R`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the XOR sum of integers from L to R.

rows.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
rows.description: Given a string `s`, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters. Solve in O(N) time using two pointers and a character index map to jump the left pointer forward immediately.
rows.outputFormat: Return an integer representing the maximum length.
rows.constraints:
0 <= s.length <= 5 * 10^4
s consists of English letters, digits, symbols and spaces.

examples.explanation: The answer is "abc", with the length of 3.
The answer is "b", with the length of 1.

rows.title: Prefix to Postfix Conversion
rows.description: Given a Prefix expression `s`, convert it to a Postfix expression using a stack. Traverse from right to left, combining `operand1 + operand2 + operator` on each operator encountered.
rows.outputFormat: Return the postfix expression string.

rows.title: Sum of Subarray Ranges
rows.description: You are given an integer array `nums`. The range of a subarray is the difference between the largest and smallest element in the subarray. Return the sum of all subarray ranges of `nums`. Solve in O(N) time using monotonic stacks: `Sum of Ranges = (Sum of Subarray Maximums) - (Sum of Subarray Minimums)`.
rows.outputFormat: Return a long integer representing total sum of ranges.

examples.explanation: Subarrays: [1] range 0; [2] range 0; [3] range 0; [1, 2] range 1; [2, 3] range 1; [1, 2, 3] range 2. Total = 4.

rows.title: Count all subsequences with sum K
rows.description: Given an array `arr` of integers and an integer `k`, count all the subsequences whose sum is equal to `k`. Since the count can be large, return it modulo 10^9 + 7.
rows.inputFormat: An integer array `arr` and an integer `k`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the number of subsequences with sum `k` modulo 10^9 + 7.

rows.title: Convert Array to Doubly Linked List
rows.description: Given an array of integers `arr`, convert it into a Doubly Linked List and return the head of the DLL in O(N) time.
rows.outputFormat: Return the head of the doubly linked list.

examples.explanation: DLL created with forward and backward links.

rows.title: Add one to a number represented by LL
rows.description: A number is represented in a linked list such that each digit corresponds to a node in linked list (MSB at head, LSB at tail). Add 1 to the number and return the head of the modified linked list. Solve in O(N) using recursion or reversing the list.
rows.inputFormat: The `head` of a linked list representing a non-negative integer.
rows.outputFormat: Return the head of the linked list after adding 1.

rows.title: Check if the i-th bit is Set or Not
rows.description: Given two integers `n` and `i`, check whether the `i`-th bit of `n` is set (1) or not (0). Use bitwise left shift `n & (1 << i)` or right shift `(n >> i) & 1`.
rows.inputFormat: Two positive integers `n` and `i` (0-indexed bit position).
rows.outputFormat: Return boolean `true` if the i-th bit is 1, else `false`.

rows.title: Longest Substring With At Most K Distinct Characters
rows.description: Given a string `s` and an integer `k`, return the length of the longest substring of `s` that contains at most `k` distinct characters. Solve in O(N) time using two pointers and a character frequency map.
rows.outputFormat: Return the maximum length of a substring with at most `k` distinct characters.

rows.title: Implement Queue using Stack
rows.description: Implement a first-in-first-out (FIFO) queue using two stacks `input` and `output`. Support `push(x)`, `pop()`, `peek()`, and `empty()`. Amortized cost for each operation must be O(1).

rows.outputFormat: Return outputs matching FIFO queue semantics.
rows.constraints:
1 <= x <= 9
At most 100 calls will be made to push, pop, peek, and empty.

rows.title: Next Greater Element - 2
rows.description: Given a circular integer array `nums` (i.e., the next element of `nums[nums.length - 1]` is `nums[0]`), return the next greater number for every element in `nums`. The next greater number of a number `x` is the first greater number to its traversing-order next in the array. If it doesn't exist, return -1. Solve in O(N) time by iterating from `2N - 1` down to `0` using a monotonic stack with index modulo `n`.

examples.explanation: The first 1's next greater number is 2; 2's is none (-1); the second 1 wraps around to find 2.
Last element 3 wraps around to find 4.

rows.title: Check for balanced binary tree
rows.description: Given a binary tree, determine if it is height-balanced. A height-balanced binary tree is defined as a binary tree in which the depth of the two subtrees of every node never differs by more than one. Solve in O(N) time by returning -1 if any subtree is unbalanced.
rows.inputFormat: The `root` node of a binary tree.
rows.outputFormat: Return boolean `true` if balanced, else `false`.
rows.constraints:
The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 5000].
-10^4 <= Node.val <= 10^4

examples.explanation: Heights of subtrees at root differ by 2 - 1 = 1 <= 1.
Subtree heights differ by more than 1.

rows.title: Word Search
rows.description: Given an `m x n` grid of characters `board` and a string `word`, return `true` if `word` exists in the grid. The word can be constructed from letters of sequentially adjacent cells (horizontally or vertically neighboring). The same letter cell may not be used more than once in a word.
rows.inputFormat: An `m x n` character grid `board` and a string `word`.
rows.outputFormat: Return boolean `true` if word exists, else `false`.
rows.constraints:
m == board.length
n = board[i].length
1 <= m, n <= 6
1 <= word.length <= 15
board and word consist of lowercase and uppercase English letters.

examples.explanation: The word "ABCCED" can be traced on the grid.

rows.title: Insertion in DLL
rows.description: Master insertion operations in a Doubly Linked List: inserting before head, inserting before tail, and inserting before the k-th node by updating four pointers in O(1) time.
rows.inputFormat: The `head` of a DLL, integer `val`, and insertion target.
rows.outputFormat: Return the head of the updated DLL.

rows.title: Merge two Sorted Lists
rows.description: You are given the heads of two sorted linked lists `list1` and `list2`. Merge the two lists into one sorted list. The list should be made by splicing together the nodes of the first two lists. Return the head of the merged linked list.
rows.inputFormat: Heads of two sorted linked lists `list1` and `list2`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the head of the merged sorted linked list.
rows.constraints:
The number of nodes in both lists is in the range [0, 50].
-100 <= Node.val <= 100
Both list1 and list2 are sorted in non-decreasing order.

rows.title: Fruit Into Baskets
rows.description: You are visiting a farm that has a single row of fruit trees arranged from left to right. The trees are represented by an integer array `fruits` where `fruits[i]` is the type of fruit the `i`-th tree produces. You only have 2 baskets, and each basket can only hold a single type of fruit. Return the maximum number of fruits you can pick (i.e. length of longest subarray with at most 2 distinct integers).
rows.outputFormat: Return the maximum fruits you can pick.

examples.explanation: We can pick from all 3 trees.

rows.title: Binary Subarrays With Sum
rows.description: Given a binary array `nums` and an integer `goal`, return the number of non-empty subarrays with a sum `goal`. Solve in O(N) time using `atMost(goal) - atMost(goal - 1)` or prefix sum hash map.
rows.inputFormat: A binary integer array `nums` and an integer `goal`.
rows.outputFormat: Return total count of binary subarrays with sum `goal`.
rows.constraints:
1 <= nums.length <= 3 * 10^4
nums[i] is either 0 or 1.
0 <= goal <= nums.length

examples.explanation: Total subarrays of all zeros is 5 * 6 / 2 = 15.

rows.title: Largest rectangle in a histogram
rows.description: Given an array of integers `heights` representing the histogram's bar height where the width of each bar is 1, return the area of the largest rectangle in the histogram. Solve in O(N) single-pass using a monotonic stack to determine width boundaries.
rows.outputFormat: Return the maximum rectangular area as an integer.

examples.explanation: The largest rectangle has height 5 and width 2 (bars at index 2 and 3), area = 5 * 2 = 10.

rows.title: LCA in BST
rows.description: Given a binary search tree (BST), find the lowest common ancestor (LCA) node of two given nodes in the BST. According to the definition of LCA, the LCA is the first split point where one target node lies in left subtree and the other in right subtree (or one node equals current node).
rows.inputFormat: The `root` of a BST and two nodes `p` and `q`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the LCA node.
rows.constraints:
The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [2, 10^5].
-10^9 <= Node.val <= 10^9
All Node.val are unique.
p != q and both exist in the BST.

examples.explanation: The LCA of nodes 2 and 8 is 6.
The LCA of nodes 2 and 4 is 2.

rows.title: Find Median from Data Stream
rows.description: The median is the middle value in an ordered integer list. Implement the `MedianFinder` class supporting `addNum(int num)` and `findMedian()` in O(log N) and O(1) time respectively using two heaps: a Max-Heap `left` for lower half and a Min-Heap `right` for upper half, keeping sizes balanced.
rows.outputFormat: Return floating-point medians.
rows.constraints:
-10^5 <= num <= 10^5
At most 5 * 10^4 calls will be made to addNum and findMedian.

rows.title: Power Set Bit Manipulation
rows.description: Given a string or array of unique characters/numbers, generate all subsets (power set) using bit manipulation. Since a set of size `n` has `2^n` subsets, iterate from `0` to `(1 << n) - 1` and inspect the j-th bit `(i & (1 << j))` to decide inclusion.
rows.inputFormat: A string `s` or array `nums` of length `n`.
rows.outputFormat: Return a list of all subsets generated in bitwise sequence.

examples.explanation: Subsets generated for bit masks from 000 to 111.

rows.title: Jump Game II
rows.description: You are given a 0-indexed array of integers `nums` of length `n`. You are initially positioned at `nums[0]`. Each element `nums[i]` represents the maximum length of a forward jump from index `i`. Return the minimum number of jumps to reach `nums[n - 1]`. You may assume that you can always reach the last index. Solve in O(N) time using BFS/greedy window approach.
rows.outputFormat: Return the minimum jump count.
rows.constraints:
1 <= nums.length <= 10^4
0 <= nums[i] <= 1000
It's guaranteed that you can reach nums[n - 1].

examples.explanation: Jump 1 step from index 0 to 1, then 3 steps to the last index. Minimum jumps = 2.

rows.title: Next Smaller Element
rows.description: Given an array `A` of integers of length `n`, find the immediate next smaller element for each element on its right side. If no smaller element exists on the right, return -1 for that position. Solve in O(N) time using a monotonic stack.
rows.outputFormat: Return an array of next smaller elements.

examples.explanation: Next smaller of 4 is 2; 5 is 2; 2 has none (-1); 10 is 8; 8 has none (-1).
Next smaller for each element found.

rows.title: Flatten Binary Tree to Linked List
rows.description: Given the `root` of a binary tree, flatten the tree into a "linked list" in-place: the "linked list" should use the same `TreeNode` class where the `right` child pointer points to the next node in the list, the `left` child pointer is always `null`, and nodes appear in preorder order. Solve in O(N) time and O(1) space using Morris traversal.
rows.outputFormat: Flatten the tree in-place so all nodes follow right child pointers.

The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 2000].
-100 <= Node.val <= 100

examples.explanation: Flattened in-place along right pointers matching preorder sequence.

rows.title: Introduction to BST
rows.description: Learn the definition and key properties of a Binary Search Tree (BST): for every node `X`, all nodes in its left subtree have `val < X.val` and all nodes in its right subtree have `val > X.val`. Understand that the Inorder traversal of any BST produces a strictly ascending sorted sequence.

rows.outputFormat: Determine BST properties and verify ordering.

rows.title: Inorder successor and predecessor in BST
rows.description: There is a BST given with root node with key part as an integer only. You need to find the in-order successor and predecessor of a given key. If either doesn't exist, return -1. Solve in O(height) time.

rows.outputFormat: Return `[predecessorVal, successorVal]`.

rows.title: Top K Frequent Elements
rows.description: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the `k` most frequent elements. You may return the answer in any order. Solve in O(N log K) time using a Min-Heap of frequency pairs or in O(N) time using Bucket Sort.

rows.constraints:
1 <= nums.length <= 10^5
-10^4 <= nums[i] <= 10^4
k is in the range [1, the number of unique elements in the array].

rows.title: Find eventual safe states

Return an array containing all the safe nodes of the graph sorted in ascending order. Solve in O(V + E) by reversing edges and applying Kahn's algorithm.

rows.title: Max Consecutive Ones III
rows.description: Given a binary array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the maximum number of consecutive `1`'s in the array if you can flip at most `k` `0`'s. Solve in O(N) time with O(1) space using a dynamic sliding window.

rows.outputFormat: Return the maximum length of consecutive 1s achievable.

nums[i] is either 0 or 1.
0 <= k <= nums.length
