examples.explanation: All trie operations succeed in linear time proportional to string length.

rows.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
rows.description: You are given a string `s` and an integer `k`. You can choose any character of the string and change it to any other uppercase English character at most `k` times. Return the length of the longest substring containing the same letter you can get after performing the above operations. Maintain `window_length - max_frequency <= k`.
rows.inputFormat: An uppercase English string `s` and integer `k`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the maximum length achievable.
rows.constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 10^5
s consists of only uppercase English letters.
0 <= k <= s.length

examples.explanation: Replace the two 'A's with two 'B's or vice versa to obtain "BBBB" or "AAAA".
Replace the middle 'A' with 'B' to form "AABBBBA". The substring "BBBB" has length 4.

rows.title: Trapping Rainwater
rows.description: Given `n` non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining. Solve in O(N) time and O(1) space using two pointers (`left` and `right`) tracking `leftMax` and `rightMax`.
rows.inputFormat: An integer array `height` representing bar elevations.
rows.outputFormat: Return the total units of trapped rainwater.

examples.explanation: The elevation map traps 6 units of rainwater.

rows.title: Check if two trees are identical or not
rows.description: Given the roots of two binary trees `p` and `q`, write a function to check if they are the same or not. Two binary trees are considered the same if they are structurally identical, and the nodes have the same value.
rows.inputFormat: Roots of two binary trees `p` and `q`.
rows.outputFormat: Return boolean `true` if identical, else `false`.
rows.constraints:
The number of nodes in both trees is in the range [0, 100].
-10^4 <= Node.val <= 10^4

examples.explanation: Both trees have identical structure and node values.

rows.title: Print root to leaf path in BT
rows.description: Given the `root` of a binary tree, return all root-to-leaf paths in any order. A leaf is a node with no children. Format each path as a string of values separated by `"->"`.
rows.outputFormat: Return a list of strings representing paths from root to each leaf.
rows.constraints:
The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 100].
-100 <= Node.val <= 100

examples.explanation: All valid root to leaf paths.

rows.title: Requirements needed to construct a unique BT
rows.description: Determine whether a unique binary tree can be constructed given two traversal sequences. Note that to construct a unique binary tree, an Inorder traversal MUST be paired with either a Preorder or Postorder traversal. Preorder + Postorder does not yield a unique tree in general.
rows.inputFormat: Two traversal sequence types `a` and `b` (e.g. 1: Preorder, 2: Inorder, 3: Postorder).
rows.outputFormat: Return boolean `true` if a unique binary tree can be constructed, else `false`.

examples.explanation: Inorder and Preorder uniquely identify root and partition left/right subtrees.
Without Inorder, left and right subtrees cannot be uniquely partitioned.

rows.title: Trie Implementation and Advanced Operations
rows.description: Implement an advanced Trie supporting counting operations: `insert(word)` in O(L), `countWordsEqualTo(word)` in O(L), `countWordsStartingWith(prefix)` in O(L), and `erase(word)` in O(L). Each node tracks `countPrefix` and `countEndsWith`.
rows.inputFormat: Method calls to Trie: insert, countWordsEqualTo, countWordsStartingWith, erase.
rows.outputFormat: Return integer counts for search queries.

examples.input: insert("apple"), insert("apple"), insert("apps"), countWordsEqualTo("apple"), countWordsStartingWith("app"), erase("apple"), countWordsEqualTo("apple")
examples.explanation: 2 "apple"s; 3 words start with "app"; after erasing one "apple", 1 remains.

rows.title: Traversal Techniques
rows.description: Master the two fundamental graph traversal algorithms: Breadth-First Search (BFS) using a FIFO queue to explore nodes level-by-level, and Depth-First Search (DFS) using recursion or an explicit stack to traverse deep into paths before backtracking. Both run in O(V + E) time.
rows.inputFormat: Number of vertices `V` and adjacency list `adj`.
rows.outputFormat: Return `[bfsTraversal, dfsTraversal]` from starting vertex 0.

examples.explanation: BFS explores immediate neighbors first; DFS explores depth first.

rows.title: Swim in Rising Water
rows.description: You are given an `n x n` integer matrix `grid` where each value `grid[i][j]` represents the elevation at that point. At time `t`, the depth of the water everywhere is `t`. You can swim to a 4-directionally adjacent cell if the water depth is at least the elevation of that cell. Return the least time until you can reach the bottom right cell `(n - 1, n - 1)` starting from `(0, 0)`. Solve in O(N^2 log N) using Dijkstra with PriorityQueue.
rows.outputFormat: Return the minimum time to swim to destination.
rows.constraints:
n == grid.length == grid[i].length
1 <= n <= 50
0 <= grid[i][j] < n^2
All values distinct.

examples.explanation: At t = 3, water level reaches 3 allowing passage to (1, 1).

rows.title: Implement Queue using Arrays
rows.description: Implement a Queue data structure using an array with front and rear pointers. Support `push(x)` to insert element x at the rear, and `pop()` to remove and return the element at the front. If the queue is empty, return -1.
rows.inputFormat: A sequence of operations: 1 x (enqueue x) and 2 (dequeue).
rows.outputFormat: Return array of values produced by pop operations.

examples.explanation: FIFO order: 2 is removed first, then 3.

rows.title: Sliding Window Maximum
rows.description: You are given an array of integers `nums`, there is a sliding window of size `k` which is moving from the very left of the array to the very right. You can only see the `k` numbers in the window. Each time the sliding window moves right by one position. Return the max sliding window. Solve in O(N) time using a monotonic decreasing deque storing indices.
rows.outputFormat: Return an array of the maximum elements in each window.

rows.title: Postorder Traversal
rows.description: Given the `root` of a binary tree, return the postorder traversal of its nodes' values (`Left -> Right -> Root`). Implement both recursive and iterative (using two stacks or 1 stack with previous pointer) versions.
rows.inputFormat: The `root` node of a binary tree.
rows.outputFormat: Return a list of integers in postorder traversal sequence.
rows.constraints:
The number of the nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 100].
-100 <= Node.val <= 100

rows.title: Correct BST with two nodes swapped
rows.description: You are given the `root` of a binary search tree (BST), where the values of exactly two nodes of the tree were swapped by mistake. Recover the tree without changing its structure. Solve in O(N) time and O(1) extra space using Morris Traversal, or O(h) space with standard Inorder recursion.
rows.inputFormat: The `root` of a BST with two swapped nodes.
rows.outputFormat: Modify the tree in-place recovering valid BST node order.
rows.constraints:
The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [2, 1000].
-2^31 <= Node.val <= 2^31 - 1

examples.explanation: 3 cannot be left child of 1. Swap 1 and 3.
2 cannot be in right subtree for root 3. Swap 2 and 3.

rows.title: Bit PreRequisites for TRIE Problems
rows.description: Learn bitwise representations required for Bitwise (Binary) Tries: bit testing `(num >> i) & 1`, maximum XOR matching (trying to branch opposite to the current bit to yield 1 in XOR), and inserting 32-bit integers from MSB (bit 31) to LSB (bit 0).
rows.outputFormat: Demonstrate binary trie prefix routing.

examples.output: Path follows bits from MSB to LSB: 0 -> ... -> 1 -> 0 -> 1
examples.explanation: Binary trie routes bits from MSB down to LSB.

rows.title: Distance of nearest cell having one
rows.description: Given an `m x n` binary matrix `grid`, find the distance of nearest 1 in the grid for each cell. The distance between two adjacent cells is 1 (Manhattan distance). Solve in O(m * n) time using multi-source BFS initialized with all cells containing 1.
rows.outputFormat: Return an `m x n` matrix where each cell has the distance to the nearest 1.
rows.constraints:
m == grid.length
n == grid[i].length
1 <= m, n <= 500
grid[i][j] is 0 or 1.
There is at least one 1 in the grid.

rows.title: Frog jump with K distances
rows.description: This is a follow-up problem to Frog Jump. Now, from stair `i`, the frog can jump up to `k` steps ahead (i.e. to `i + 1`, `i + 2`, ..., `i + k`). Find the minimum total energy lost by the frog to reach the `n`-th stair. Solve in O(N * K) time with O(K) space.
rows.inputFormat: An integer array `height` of length `n` and an integer `k`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the minimum energy spent.

examples.explanation: Jump from index 0 to 1 (cost 20), then 1 to 4 (cost 10). Total = 30.

rows.title: Subset sum equals to target
rows.description: Given an array of non-negative integers `nums` and a value `target`, determine if there is a subset of the given array with sum equal to given `target`. Solve in O(N * target) time and O(target) space using dynamic programming: `dp[j] = dp[j] || dp[j - nums[i]]`.
rows.outputFormat: Return boolean `true` if subset sum equals target, else `false`.

rows.title: Stock span problem
rows.description: Design an algorithm that collects daily price quotes for some stock and returns the span of that stock's price for the current day. The span of the stock's price today is defined as the maximum number of consecutive days (starting from today and going backward) for which the stock price was less than or equal to today's price. Solve in amortized O(1) time per day using a monotonic stack of `(price, span)` pairs.
rows.inputFormat: A series of calls to StockSpanner.next(price).
rows.outputFormat: Return an array of span values.
rows.constraints:
1 <= price <= 10^5
At most 10^4 calls will be made to next.

examples.input: next(100), next(80), next(60), next(70), next(60), next(75), next(85)

examples.explanation: Prices strictly increase, giving consecutive spans.

rows.title: Maximum Depth in BT
rows.description: Given the `root` of a binary tree, return its maximum depth. A binary tree's maximum depth is the number of nodes along the longest path from the root node down to the farthest leaf node. Compute recursively using `1 + max(maxDepth(left), maxDepth(right))`.
rows.inputFormat: The `root` node of a binary tree.
rows.outputFormat: Return an integer representing the maximum depth.
rows.constraints:
The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 10^4].
-100 <= Node.val <= 100

rows.title: Construct a BT from Preorder and Inorder
rows.description: Given two integer arrays `preorder` and `inorder` where `preorder` is the preorder traversal of a binary tree and `inorder` is the inorder traversal of the same tree, construct and return the binary tree. Use a hash map of inorder indices to divide subtrees in O(N) time.
rows.outputFormat: Return the `root` node of the constructed binary tree.
rows.constraints:
1 <= preorder.length <= 3000
inorder.length == preorder.length
-3000 <= preorder[i], inorder[i] <= 3000
preorder and inorder consist of unique values.

examples.explanation: Root is 3. Inorder shows 9 in left subtree and [15, 20, 7] in right subtree.

rows.title: Check if an array represents a min heap
rows.description: Given an array `arr` of size `n`, check whether it represents a Min-Heap (i.e. every parent node at index `i` satisfies `arr[i] <= arr[2*i + 1]` and `arr[i] <= arr[2*i + 2]`).
rows.outputFormat: Return boolean `true` if valid min-heap, else `false`.

examples.explanation: 10 <= 15 and 10 <= 14; 15 <= 25 and 15 <= 30. All parent-child relations valid.
Parent 25 is greater than child 20 at index 3.

rows.title: Number of islands
rows.description: Given an `m x n` 2D binary grid `grid` which represents a map of `'1'`s (land) and `'0'`s (water), return the number of islands. An island is surrounded by water and is formed by connecting adjacent lands horizontally or vertically. Solve in O(m * n) time using BFS or DFS flood-fill.
rows.inputFormat: An `m x n` 2D grid of '1's and '0's.
rows.outputFormat: Return the total count of islands.
rows.constraints:
m == grid.length
n == grid[i].length
1 <= m, n <= 300
grid[i][j] is '0' or '1'.

examples.explanation: All '1's are connected together into a single island.

rows.title: Detect a cycle in a directed graph
rows.description: Given a Directed Graph with `V` vertices and `E` edges, determine if it contains any cycle. Solve in O(V + E) time using DFS with a path-visited recursion stack, or using Kahn's Algorithm (if topological sort count < V, then a cycle exists).
rows.inputFormat: An integer `V` and adjacency list `adj` of a directed graph.
rows.outputFormat: Return boolean `true` if cycle exists, else `false`.

rows.title: Disjoint Set
rows.description: Implement the Disjoint Set Union (DSU / Union-Find) data structure with two crucial optimizations: Path Compression in `findUPar(u)` and Union by Rank (or Size) in `unionByRank(u, v)`. These optimizations reduce the amortized time complexity of union and find operations to nearly constant time `O(alpha(N))` (inverse Ackermann function).
rows.inputFormat: Number of elements `n` and union/find query commands.
rows.outputFormat: Return results of find queries and component groupings.

examples.explanation: 1 and 3 belong to the same connected set.

rows.title: Maximum Rectangles
rows.description: Given a `rows x cols` binary `matrix` filled with 0's and 1's, find the largest rectangle containing only 1's and return its area. Solve in O(rows * cols) time by converting each row into an accumulated histogram and applying the Largest Rectangle in Histogram algorithm.
rows.outputFormat: Return the maximum area of a rectangle of 1s.
rows.constraints:
rows == matrix.length
cols == matrix[i].length
1 <= rows, cols <= 200
matrix[i][j] is '0' or '1'.

examples.explanation: The maximal rectangle has area 6 (height 2, width 3).

rows.title: LRU Cache
rows.description: Design a data structure that follows the constraints of a Least Recently Used (LRU) cache. Implement the `LRUCache` class with `get(key)` in O(1) time and `put(key, value)` in O(1) time. When the cache reaches its capacity, it should invalidate and evict the least recently used key before inserting a new item. Use a Doubly Linked List paired with a Hash Map.
rows.inputFormat: Method calls to LRUCache: LRUCache(capacity), put(key, value), get(key).
rows.outputFormat: Return outputs matching LRU eviction semantics.
rows.constraints:
1 <= capacity <= 3000
0 <= key <= 10^4
0 <= value <= 10^5
At most 2 * 10^5 calls to get and put.

examples.input: LRUCache(2), put(1, 1), put(2, 2), get(1), put(3, 3), get(2), put(4, 4), get(1), get(3), get(4)
examples.explanation: Key 2 is evicted when key 3 is added. Later key 1 is evicted when key 4 is added.

rows.title: Kth Smallest and Largest element in BST
rows.description: Given the `root` of a binary search tree, and an integer `k`, return the `k`-th smallest value and `k`-th largest value in the tree. Since Inorder traversal is sorted, the k-th node visited during Inorder is the k-th smallest element, and reverse Inorder gives k-th largest.
rows.inputFormat: The `root` of a BST and an integer `k`.
rows.outputFormat: Return `[kthSmallest, kthLargest]`.
rows.constraints:
The number of nodes in the tree is n.
1 <= k <= n <= 10^4
0 <= Node.val <= 10^4

rows.title: Sort a K-Sorted Array
rows.description: Given an array `arr` of `n` elements, where each element is at most `k` positions away from its target position in the sorted array. Sort the array in O(N log K) time using a Min-Heap of size `k + 1`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the completely sorted array.

rows.title: Flood fill algorithm
rows.description: An image is represented by an `m x n` integer grid `image` where `image[i][j]` represents the pixel value of the image. You are given three integers `sr`, `sc`, and `color`. You should perform a flood fill on the image starting from pixel `image[sr][sc]`. To perform a flood fill, consider the starting pixel, plus any 4-directionally connected pixels with the same color, and update them to the new `color`. Solve in O(m * n) using BFS or DFS.
rows.inputFormat: An `m x n` 2D integer matrix `image`, starting coordinates `(sr, sc)`, and target `color`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the modified image matrix after flood fill.
rows.constraints:
m == image.length
n == image[i].length
1 <= m, n <= 50
0 <= image[i][j], color < 2^16
0 <= sr < m
0 <= sc < n

examples.explanation: From the center at (1, 1), all connected pixels with value 1 are filled with color 2.
Starting pixel is already color 0, so no changes occur.

rows.title: Alien Dictionary
rows.description: There is a new alien language that uses the English alphabet. However, the order among letters is unknown. You are given a list of strings `words` from the alien language's dictionary, where the strings are sorted lexicographically by the rules of this new language. Derive the order of letters in this alien language. If no valid order exists, return `""`. Construct a directed graph from adjacent word mismatches and compute Topological Sort.
rows.inputFormat: An array of strings `words` and integer `k` (alphabet size).
rows.outputFormat: Return a string representing the alien alphabetical order.

examples.explanation: From "baa" and "abcd", b comes before a; "abcd" and "abca" gives d before a; "abca" and "cab" gives a before c; "cab" and "cad" gives b before d.

rows.title: Number of operations to make network connected
rows.description: There are `n` computers numbered from `0` to `n - 1` connected by ethernet cables `connections`. You can extract certain cables and reconnect them between any pair of disconnected computers. Return the minimum number of times you need to do this in order to make all the computers connected. If it is impossible, return -1. Use Disjoint Set Union to count redundant cables and total components.
rows.outputFormat: Return minimum operations, or -1 if impossible.

examples.explanation: Remove redundant cable [1, 2] and connect computer 3. Total 1 move.
Not enough cables to connect 6 computers.

rows.title: Asteroid Collision
rows.description: We are given an array `asteroids` of integers representing asteroids in a row. The absolute value represents size, and sign represents direction (+ moving right, - moving left). Each asteroid moves at the same speed. Find out the state of the asteroids after all collisions using a stack. Two asteroids moving towards each other collide: smaller explodes, equal sizes both explode, larger continues.
rows.outputFormat: Return the surviving asteroids in order.

examples.explanation: 10 and -5 collide resulting in 10 surviving. 5 and 10 never collide.

rows.title: Inorder Traversal
rows.description: Given the `root` of a binary tree, return the inorder traversal of its nodes' values (`Left -> Root -> Right`). Implement both recursive and iterative versions using an explicit stack.
rows.inputFormat: The `root` node of a binary tree.
rows.outputFormat: Return a list of node values in inorder sequence.
rows.constraints:
The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 100].
-100 <= Node.val <= 100

examples.explanation: Inorder traversal visits Left -> Root -> Right.

rows.title: Check for symmetrical BTs
rows.description: Given the `root` of a binary tree, check whether it is a mirror of itself (i.e., symmetric around its center). A tree is symmetric if `left.val == right.val` and left's left subtree matches right's right subtree while left's right matches right's left.
rows.inputFormat: The `root` node of a binary tree.
rows.outputFormat: Return boolean `true` if symmetric, else `false`.
rows.constraints:
The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 1000].
-100 <= Node.val <= 100

examples.explanation: The tree is symmetric around its vertical axis.
Left and right subtrees do not mirror each other.

rows.title: Morris Preorder Traversal
rows.description: Given the `root` of a binary tree, return the preorder traversal of its nodes' values using Morris Preorder Traversal in O(N) time and strictly O(1) auxiliary space. When establishing a thread to the predecessor, record the current node value before moving left.
rows.outputFormat: Return a list of integers in preorder sequence with O(1) auxiliary space.

examples.explanation: Preorder sequence generated using threaded tree pointers.

rows.title: Minimum Cost to Connect Sticks
rows.description: You have some number of sticks with positive integer lengths. You can connect any two sticks of lengths `x` and `y` into one stick by paying a cost of `x + y`. You perform this until there is only one stick remaining. Return the minimum cost of connecting all the given sticks. Solve in O(N log N) using a Min-Heap (Huffman Coding principle).
rows.outputFormat: Return the minimum connection cost as an integer.

examples.explanation: Connect 2 and 3 for cost 5 -> [4, 5]. Connect 4 and 5 for cost 9 -> [9]. Total cost = 5 + 9 = 14.

rows.title: Number of distinct islands
rows.description: Given a boolean 2D matrix `grid` of size `n x m`. You have to find the number of distinct islands where a group of connected 1s forms an island. Two islands are considered distinct if one cannot be translated (shifted) into the other. Solve by recording the relative coordinates `(r - r0, c - c0)` of each island in a HashSet.
rows.outputFormat: Return the number of distinct island shapes.

examples.explanation: Both islands are 2x2 squares, so they have the identical shape. Total distinct = 1.

rows.title: Bellman ford algorithm
rows.description: Given a weighted, directed graph of `V` vertices and `E` edges with source `S`, find the shortest distance from `S` to all vertices. Unlike Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford can handle negative weights and detect negative weight cycles. Relax all edges `V - 1` times in O(V * E) time. If an edge can still be relaxed on the `V`-th pass, a negative cycle exists (return `[-1]`).
rows.inputFormat: An integer `V`, edge list `edges` containing `[u, v, weight]`, and source `S`.
rows.outputFormat: Return an array of shortest distances, or [-1] if a negative cycle is detected.

examples.explanation: Shortest distance from 2 to all vertices computed.

rows.title: Unbounded knapsack
rows.description: Given a set of `N` items, each with a weight and a value, represented by the array `wt` and `val` respectively. Also, a knapsack with weight limit `W`. The task is to fill the knapsack in such a way that we can get the maximum profit. Return the maximum profit. Note: each item can be taken any number of times (unbounded).
rows.outputFormat: Return maximum value achievable.

examples.explanation: Pick item 2 three times (weight 9, value 90) and item 1 once (weight 1, value 1). Or pick item 2 with 30/3 = 10 ratio 3 times.

rows.title: Diameter of Binary Tree
rows.description: Given the `root` of a binary tree, return the length of the diameter of the tree. The diameter of a binary tree is the length of the longest path between any two nodes in a tree. This path may or may not pass through the root. Solve in O(N) time maintaining `max(diameter, leftHeight + rightHeight)`.
rows.inputFormat: The `root` node of a binary tree.
rows.outputFormat: Return the diameter length (number of edges on longest path).
rows.constraints:
The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 10^4].
-100 <= Node.val <= 100

examples.explanation: 3 is the length of the path [4, 2, 1, 3] or [5, 2, 1, 3].

rows.title: Check if a tree is a BST or not
rows.description: Given the `root` of a binary tree, determine if it is a valid binary search tree (BST). A valid BST satisfies: left subtree values < current node val < right subtree values across all levels. Solve recursively passing valid range `(minVal, maxVal)` in O(N) time.
rows.outputFormat: Return boolean `true` if valid BST, else `false`.
rows.constraints:
The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 10^4].
-2^31 <= Node.val <= 2^31 - 1

examples.explanation: The root's right child is 4, which is less than 5.

rows.title: Heap Sort
rows.description: Given an array of size `n`, sort the array in non-decreasing order using Heap Sort in O(N log N) time and O(1) extra space. Steps: 1. Build a Max-Heap from the array in O(N). 2. Repeatedly swap the root with the last element, reduce heap size, and Max-Heapify root.
rows.inputFormat: An unsorted integer array `nums` of length `n`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the array sorted in ascending order.

rows.title: Count subsets with sum K
rows.description: Given an array `nums` of non-negative integers and an integer `k`, count the number of subsets with sum equal to `k`. Since the answer may be large, return it modulo 10^9 + 7. Be mindful of zeros in the input which double the number of valid subsets.
rows.inputFormat: An integer array `nums` and target integer `k`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the total count of subsets modulo 10^9 + 7.

examples.explanation: Four subsets due to inclusion/exclusion of zeros.

rows.title: Level Order Traversal
rows.description: Given the `root` of a binary tree, return the level order traversal of its nodes' values (i.e., from left to right, level by level) using a FIFO queue (BFS).
rows.inputFormat: The `root` node of a binary tree.
rows.outputFormat: Return a list of lists of integers, where each sublist contains values of a tree level.
rows.constraints:
The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 2000].
-1000 <= Node.val <= 1000

examples.explanation: Level 0 has [3], Level 1 has [9, 20], Level 2 has [15, 7].

rows.title: Print all nodes at a distance of K in BT
rows.description: Given the `root` of a binary tree, the value of a target node `target`, and an integer `k`, return an array of the values of all nodes that have a distance `k` from the target node. Solve by establishing child-to-parent pointers with BFS/DFS and running a radial BFS outward up to distance `k`.
rows.outputFormat: Return a list of node values at distance `k`.
rows.constraints:
The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 500].
0 <= Node.val <= 500
All values are unique.
0 <= k <= 1000

examples.explanation: Nodes that are distance 2 from node 5 are 7, 4, and 1.

rows.title: Morris Inorder Traversal
rows.description: Given the `root` of a binary tree, return the inorder traversal of its nodes' values using Morris Inorder Traversal in O(N) time and strictly O(1) auxiliary space by creating temporary threaded links from the inorder predecessor to current node.
rows.outputFormat: Return a list of integers in inorder sequence with O(1) space.

examples.explanation: Traversal accomplished in O(1) space without recursion or stack.

rows.title: Implement Min Heap
rows.description: Implement a Min-Heap data structure with methods: `insert(val)` in O(log N) time using sift-up, `extractMin()` in O(log N) time using sift-down, and `getMin()` in O(1) time.
rows.outputFormat: Return array of values returned by extractMin queries.

examples.explanation: First min is 2. After inserting 1, new min is 1.

rows.title: Replace Elements by Their Rank
rows.description: Given an array of `n` integers, replace each element with its rank in the array. The rank of an element is an integer starting from 1. If two elements are equal, they have the same rank, and ranks are consecutive without skipping. Solve in O(N log N) using a Min-Heap or sorting distinct elements.
rows.outputFormat: Return an array of the same size with elements replaced by their ranks.

rows.title: Count primes in range L to R
rows.description: Given two integers `L` and `R`, find the total count of prime numbers in the range `[L, R]` inclusive. Solve in O(R log(log R)) using prefix prime counts from a precomputed Sieve of Eratosthenes, or Segmented Sieve for large ranges.
rows.inputFormat: Two positive integers `L` and `R` where `L <= R`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the number of prime numbers in range [L, R].

rows.title: Shortest path in DAG
rows.description: Given a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) with `V` vertices and `E` weighted edges, find the shortest path from a given source vertex `src = 0` to all other vertices. If a vertex is unreachable, return -1 for its distance. Solve in O(V + E) time by computing Topological Sort first, then relaxing edges in topological order.
rows.inputFormat: An integer `V`, integer `E`, and edge list with `(u, v, weight)`.
rows.outputFormat: Return an array of shortest distances from vertex 0 to all vertices.

examples.explanation: Shortest distances from source 0 to vertices 0 through 5.

rows.title: Find the MST weight
rows.description: Given a weighted, undirected and connected graph of `V` vertices and `E` edges, find the sum of weights of the edges of the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST). Implement Prim's algorithm using a Min-Heap in O(E log V) or Kruskal's algorithm using Disjoint Set Union in O(E log E) time.
rows.inputFormat: Number of vertices `V` and adjacency list `adj`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the sum of weights of edges in the MST.

examples.explanation: Edges (0, 2) weight 1 and (1, 2) weight 3 give MST weight 4.

rows.title: Boundary Traversal
rows.description: Given a Binary Tree, find its Boundary Traversal. The boundary includes: 1. Left boundary nodes (excluding leaves). 2. All leaf nodes (left to right). 3. Right boundary nodes in reverse bottom-up order (excluding leaves).
rows.outputFormat: Return a list of node values along the boundary in anti-clockwise order.

examples.explanation: Anti-clockwise traversal: left boundary, leaves, and reverse right boundary.

rows.title: Serialize and De-serialize BT
rows.description: Serialization is the process of converting a data structure or object into a sequence of bits or a string so that it can be stored. Deserialization reconstructs the tree from this string. Design an algorithm to serialize and deserialize a binary tree using Level Order traversal (BFS) with comma separation and `'#'` for null nodes.
rows.inputFormat: A binary tree for `serialize(root)` and a string for `deserialize(data)`.
rows.outputFormat: The reconstructed tree must match the original tree identically.
rows.constraints:
The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 10^4].
-1000 <= Node.val <= 1000

examples.explanation: Serialized string can be deserialized back into identical binary tree.
Empty tree serializes to empty string.

rows.title: Largest BST in Binary Tree
rows.description: Given a binary tree, find the largest subtree which is also a Binary Search Tree (BST), where the largest means subtree with the largest number of nodes in it. A subtree must include all of its descendants. Solve in O(N) postorder time by passing `(size, minVal, maxVal)` up from children.
rows.outputFormat: Return the size (number of nodes) of the largest BST subtree.
rows.constraints:
The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 10^4].
-10^4 <= Node.val <= 10^4

examples.explanation: Subtree rooted at 5 with nodes [5, 1, 8] is a valid BST of size 3.

examples.input: root = [4, 2, 7, 2, 3, 5, null, 2, null, null, null, null, null, 1]

rows.title: Kth largest element in a stream of running integers
rows.description: Design a class to find the `k`-th largest element in a stream. Note that it is the `k`-th largest element in the sorted order, not the `k`-th distinct element. Implement `KthLargest` class with constructor and `add(val)` method in O(log k) time using a Min-Heap of size `k`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the current k-th largest element after each insertion.
rows.constraints:
1 <= k <= 10^4
0 <= nums.length <= 10^4
-10^4 <= val <= 10^4
At most 10^4 calls to add.

examples.input: KthLargest(3, [4, 5, 8, 2]), add(3), add(5), add(10), add(9), add(4)
examples.explanation: After add(3): [2, 3, 4, 5, 8] -> 3rd largest is 4; add(5): 3rd largest is 5, etc.

rows.title: Number of provinces
rows.description: There are `n` cities. Some of them are connected, while some are not. If city `a` is connected directly with city `b`, and city `b` is connected directly with city `c`, then city `a` is connected indirectly with city `c`. A province is a group of directly or indirectly connected cities. Given an `n x n` adjacency matrix `isConnected`, return the total number of provinces. Solve in O(V^2) using DFS/BFS or Disjoint Set Union.
rows.outputFormat: Return the total number of provinces.
rows.constraints:
1 <= n <= 200
isConnected[i][j] is 1 or 0.
isConnected[i][i] == 1
isConnected[i][j] == isConnected[j][i]

examples.explanation: Cities 0 and 1 form one province, and city 2 forms another.
All 3 cities are isolated, giving 3 provinces.

rows.title: Surrounded Regions
rows.description: Given an `m x n` matrix `board` containing `'X'` and `'O'`, capture all regions that are 4-directionally surrounded by `'X'`. A region is captured by flipping all `'O'`s into `'X'`s in that surrounded region. An `'O'` cell on the boundary or connected to the boundary cannot be captured. Solve in O(m * n) using boundary BFS/DFS.
rows.outputFormat: Modify the matrix in-place with surrounded 'O's flipped to 'X's.
rows.constraints:
m == board.length
n == board[i].length
1 <= m, n <= 200
board[i][j] is 'X' or 'O'.

examples.explanation: Only the 'O' at (3, 1) touches the boundary and survives; all others are captured.

rows.title: MST theory
rows.description: Learn the principles of Minimum Spanning Trees (MST) in connected, weighted undirected graphs. An MST is a subgraph that connects all `V` vertices with exactly `V - 1` edges without cycles and with the minimum total edge weight. Learn Cut Property, Cycle Property, Prim's Greedy Algorithm, and Kruskal's Algorithm.
rows.outputFormat: Understand MST properties and edge count = V - 1.

examples.explanation: Spanning tree connects all 4 nodes with 3 edges.

rows.title: Maximum Width of BT
rows.description: Given the `root` of a binary tree, return the maximum width of the given tree. The maximum width of a tree is the maximum width among all levels. The width of one level is defined as the length between the end-nodes (the leftmost and rightmost non-null nodes), where the null nodes between the end-nodes are counted as if in a full binary tree. Index nodes as `2*i + 1` and `2*i + 2` using BFS.
rows.outputFormat: Return an integer representing the maximum width.
rows.constraints:
The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 3000].
-100 <= Node.val <= 100

examples.explanation: The maximum width exists in the third level with nodes [5, 3, null, 9] (width 4).

rows.title: Search in BST
rows.description: You are given the `root` of a binary search tree (BST) and an integer `val`. Find the node in the BST that the node's value equals `val` and return the subtree rooted with that node. If such a node does not exist, return `null`. Solve in O(height) time.
rows.inputFormat: The `root` of a BST and integer `val`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the subtree rooted at target node, or null.
rows.constraints:
The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 5000].
1 <= Node.val <= 10^7
root is a valid BST.

examples.explanation: Node 2 with its subtree [2, 1, 3] is returned.

rows.title: Heapify Algorithm
rows.description: Given an array representing a binary tree and an index `i`, write a function `heapify` that maintains the heap property (either Min-Heapify or Max-Heapify) by sifting down the element at index `i` in O(log N) time.
rows.inputFormat: An integer array `nums` and root index `i` of subtree.
rows.outputFormat: Modify `nums` in-place maintaining the heap invariant.

examples.explanation: 4 swapped with larger child 10, then with 5 to restore max-heap.

rows.title: Detect a cycle in an undirected graph
rows.description: Given an undirected graph with `V` vertices and `E` edges, determine whether the graph contains any cycle or not. Solve in O(V + E) time using BFS or DFS tracking the parent node of each visited vertex.
rows.outputFormat: Return boolean `true` if cycle exists, else `false`.

examples.explanation: Nodes 0, 1, and 2 form a cycle triangle.
Linear chain graph has no cycle.

rows.title: Path with minimum effort
rows.description: Determine the path from `(0, 0)` to `(m - 1, n - 1)` in a grid that minimizes the maximum effort (maximum height jump between adjacent cells). Solve in O(rows * cols * log(rows * cols)) using Dijkstra with a priority queue.
rows.inputFormat: A 2D integer matrix `heights` of size `m x n`.
rows.outputFormat: Return an integer representing the minimized maximum jump.

examples.explanation: Path through only 1s has maximum difference 0.

rows.title: Best time to buy and sell stock with transaction fees
rows.description: You are given an array `prices` representing stock prices and an integer `fee` representing a transaction fee. You may complete as many transactions as you like, but you need to pay the transaction fee for each transaction. Return the maximum profit you can achieve. Solve in O(N) time and O(1) space.
rows.inputFormat: An integer array `prices` and an integer `fee`.
rows.outputFormat: Return maximum profit after fees.

examples.explanation: Buy at 1, sell at 8 (profit 8-1-2 = 5). Buy at 4, sell at 9 (profit 9-4-2 = 3). Total = 8.

rows.title: Bottom view of BT
rows.description: Given a binary tree, return an array of nodes representing the bottom view of the tree from leftmost column to rightmost. If there are multiple bottom-most nodes for a horizontal distance, the node that appears later in level order traversal is considered.
rows.outputFormat: Return a list of node values representing the bottom view.

examples.explanation: Bottom-most nodes at each horizontal column are visible.

rows.title: Delete a node in BST
rows.description: Given a root node reference of a BST and a `key`, delete the node with the given key in the BST. Return the root node reference of the BST. Deletion involves 3 cases: 1. Node is leaf (remove directly). 2. Node has 1 child (link child to parent). 3. Node has 2 children (replace with inorder successor or predecessor and delete it).
rows.inputFormat: The `root` of a BST and integer `key`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the `root` after deleting `key`.
rows.constraints:
The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 10^4].
-10^5 <= Node.val, key <= 10^5
All values are unique.

examples.explanation: Node 3 is deleted and replaced with its inorder successor 4.
Key 0 does not exist in BST, so tree remains unchanged.

rows.title: BST iterator
rows.description: Implement the `BSTIterator` class that represents an iterator over the in-order traversal of a binary search tree (BST). Support `next()` returning the next smallest number, and `hasNext()` returning boolean. `next()` must run in amortized O(1) time and use O(h) memory where `h` is tree height.
rows.inputFormat: Method calls to BSTIterator initialized with tree root.
rows.outputFormat: Return in-order values sequentially.
rows.constraints:
The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 10^5].
0 <= Node.val <= 10^6
At most 10^5 calls to next and hasNext.

examples.input: BSTIterator([7, 3, 15, null, null, 9, 20]), next(), next(), hasNext(), next(), hasNext(), next(), hasNext(), next(), hasNext()
examples.explanation: Yields values in ascending sorted order: 3, 7, 9, 15, 20.

rows.title: Maximum XOR of two numbers in an array
rows.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return the maximum result of `nums[i] XOR nums[j]`, where `0 <= i <= j < n`. Solve in O(32 * N) time using a Binary Trie by inserting all numbers and querying maximum XOR greedy bit branching.
rows.outputFormat: Return the maximum XOR value.

rows.title: Topological sort or Kahn's algorithm
rows.description: Given a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) with `V` vertices and `E` edges, find any Topological Sorting of that graph. Topological sorting for DAG is a linear ordering of vertices such that for every directed edge `u -> v`, vertex `u` comes before `v` in the ordering. Solve in O(V + E) time using Kahn's algorithm (BFS with in-degrees) or DFS with a stack.
rows.inputFormat: An integer `V` and adjacency list `adj` of a DAG.
rows.outputFormat: Return an array representing a valid topological sort sequence.

examples.explanation: All edges point from left to right in this topological order.

rows.title: Floyd warshall algorithm
rows.description: The problem is to find the shortest distance between all pairs of vertices in a given directed weighted graph. The graph is represented as an adjacency matrix of size `n x n`. If a path does not exist, value is -1. Solve in O(V^3) time using the Floyd-Warshall dynamic programming algorithm: `matrix[i][j] = min(matrix[i][j], matrix[i][k] + matrix[k][j])`.
rows.outputFormat: Modify `matrix` in-place with all-pairs shortest distances.

examples.explanation: Shortest distance from 0 to 2 is through 1: 1 + 6 = 7.

rows.title: Frog Jump
rows.description: Given an array of heights of `n` stairs. A frog is initially at the 1st stair (index 0). At any stair `i`, the frog can jump to either stair `i + 1` or stair `i + 2`. The energy lost in jumping from stair `i` to `j` is `|height[i] - height[j]|`. Find the minimum total energy lost by the frog to reach the `n`-th stair (index n - 1). Solve in O(N) time and O(1) space.
rows.outputFormat: Return the minimum energy spent as an integer.

examples.explanation: Jump from 0 to 1 (energy 10) and 1 to 3 (energy 10). Total = 20.
Jump directly from 0 to 2 with energy |10 - 10| = 0.

rows.title: Hand of Straights
rows.description: Alice has some number of cards and she wants to rearrange the cards into groups so that each group is of size `groupSize`, and consists of `groupSize` consecutive cards. Given an integer array `hand` and an integer `groupSize`, return `true` if she can rearrange the cards, or `false` otherwise. Solve in O(N log N) using a TreeMap or Min-Heap with frequency map.
rows.outputFormat: Return boolean `true` if grouping is possible, else `false`.

examples.explanation: Cards can be grouped into [1, 2, 3], [2, 3, 4], and [6, 7, 8].
Cannot divide 5 cards into groups of 4.

rows.title: Maximum Xor with an element from an array
rows.description: You are given an array `nums` and an array `queries` where `queries[i] = [x_i, m_i]`. The answer to the i-th query is the maximum bitwise XOR value of `x_i` with any element of `nums` that does not exceed `m_i`. If all elements exceed `m_i`, answer is -1. Solve in O((N + Q) * log(max) + Q log Q) time using offline query sorting and an incremental Binary Trie.
rows.inputFormat: An integer array `nums` and array of queries `[x, m]`.
rows.outputFormat: Return an array of answers for each query.
rows.constraints:
1 <= nums.length, queries.length <= 10^5
queries[i].length == 2
0 <= nums[j], x_i, m_i <= 10^9

examples.explanation: For [8, 1], no element in nums is <= 1, so answer is -1.

rows.title: Word ladder I
rows.description: A transformation sequence from word `beginWord` to word `endWord` using a dictionary `wordList` is a sequence of words `beginWord -> s1 -> s2 -> ... -> sk` such that every adjacent pair of words differs by exactly one letter. Return the number of words in the shortest transformation sequence from `beginWord` to `endWord`, or 0 if no such sequence exists. Solve in O(N * L * 26) using BFS with a HashSet of dictionary words.
rows.inputFormat: Two strings `beginWord` and `endWord`, and a list of strings `wordList`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the integer length of the shortest transformation sequence.
rows.constraints:
1 <= beginWord.length <= 10
endWord.length == beginWord.length
1 <= wordList.length <= 5000
All words have the same length and lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: One shortest transformation sequence is "hit" -> "hot" -> "dot" -> "dog" -> "cog", which is 5 words long.
The endWord "cog" is not in wordList.

rows.title: Cheapest flight within K stops
rows.description: There are `n` cities connected by some number of flights. You are given an array `flights` where `flights[i] = [from_i, to_i, price_i]`. You are also given three integers `src`, `dst`, and `k`, return the cheapest price from `src` to `dst` with at most `k` stops. If there is no such route, return -1. Solve in O(k * E) using a queue with `(stops, node, cost)` or Bellman-Ford.
rows.outputFormat: Return the minimum cost, or -1.
rows.constraints:
1 <= n <= 100
0 <= flights.length <= (n * (n - 1) / 2)
0 <= src, dst < n
0 <= k < n

examples.explanation: Cheapest path with at most 1 stop is 0 -> 1 -> 3 with cost 100 + 600 = 700.

rows.title: Most stones removed with same row or column
rows.description: On a 2D plane, we place `n` stones at some integer coordinate points. Each coordinate point may have at most one stone. A stone can be removed if it shares either the same row or the same column as another stone that has not been removed. Return the largest possible number of stones that can be removed. Formula: `totalStones - totalConnectedComponents` using Disjoint Set Union.
rows.outputFormat: Return maximum removable stones count.
rows.constraints:
1 <= stones.length <= 1000
0 <= x_i, y_i <= 10^4
No two stones at same position.

examples.explanation: All stones form a single connected component of size 6. We can remove 6 - 1 = 5 stones.

rows.title: Best time to buy and sell stock II
rows.description: You are given an integer array `prices` where `prices[i]` is the price of a given stock on the `i`-th day. On each day, you may decide to buy and/or sell the stock. You can only hold at most one share of the stock at any time. Find and return the maximum profit you can achieve. Solve in O(N) time using DP or greedy accumulation of all positive price differences.
rows.outputFormat: Return the maximum profit achievable with unlimited transactions.

examples.explanation: Buy on day 2 (price 1) and sell on day 3 (price 5), profit = 4. Buy on day 4 (price 3) and sell on day 5 (price 6), profit = 3. Total profit = 4 + 3 = 7.
Buy on day 1 and sell on day 5, profit = 4.

rows.title: Task Scheduler
rows.description: Given a characters array `tasks`, representing the CPU tasks a processor needs to do, where each letter represents a different task. Tasks could be done in any order. Each task is done in one unit of time. There is a non-negative integer `n` that represents the cooldown period between two same tasks. Return the least number of units of times that the CPU will take to finish all the given tasks. Solve in O(tasks.length) using Max-Heap or math formula `(maxFreq - 1) * (n + 1) + countMaxFreq`.
rows.inputFormat: A character array `tasks` and an integer `n`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the minimum CPU intervals needed.
rows.constraints:
1 <= tasks.length <= 10^4
tasks[i] is uppercase English letter.
0 <= n <= 100

examples.explanation: A -> B -> idle -> A -> B -> idle -> A -> B. Total = 8 units.

rows.title: Connected Components
rows.description: Given an undirected graph with `V` vertices and an adjacency list, find the number of connected components. A connected component is a maximal set of vertices such that every pair is connected by a path. Iterate through all vertices and trigger BFS or DFS for unvisited vertices in O(V + E) time.
rows.outputFormat: Return the number of connected components as an integer.

rows.title: Bipartite graph
rows.description: There is an undirected graph with `n` nodes. A graph is bipartite if the nodes can be partitioned into two independent sets `A` and `B` such that every edge connects a node in set `A` and a node in set `B`. Return `true` if and only if it is bipartite. Note: a graph is bipartite if and only if it does not contain an odd-length cycle. Solve in O(V + E) time using 2-coloring BFS or DFS.
rows.inputFormat: A 2D integer array `graph` where `graph[u]` is an array of nodes that node `u` is adjacent to.
rows.outputFormat: Return boolean `true` if bipartite, else `false`.
rows.constraints:
graph.length == n
1 <= n <= 100
0 <= graph[u].length < n
No self-loops or parallel edges.

examples.explanation: Cannot partition nodes into two sets because of odd cycle between 0, 1, 2.
Even cycle of 4 nodes can be colored with 2 colors: {0, 2} and {1, 3}.

rows.title: Shortest Distance in a Binary Maze
rows.description: You are a hiker preparing for an upcoming hike. You are given `heights`, a 2D array of size `rows x columns`, where `heights[row][col]` represents the height of cell `(row, col)`. You can move up, down, left, or right. A path's effort is the maximum absolute difference in heights between two consecutive cells of the path. Return the minimum effort required to travel from `(0, 0)` to `(rows - 1, columns - 1)` using Dijkstra's algorithm.
rows.outputFormat: Return the minimum effort value.
rows.constraints:
rows == heights.length
columns == heights[i].length
1 <= rows, columns <= 100
1 <= heights[i][j] <= 10^6

examples.explanation: Path along perimeter has maximum difference of only 1.

rows.title: Ninja's training
rows.description: Ninja is planning this `n` days-long training schedule. Each day he can perform any one of 3 activities: Running (0), Fighting (1), or Learning (2). Each activity on day `i` earns him points given by `points[i][0]`, `points[i][1]`, and `points[i][2]`. Ninja cannot perform the same activity on two consecutive days. Find the maximum merit points Ninja can earn. Solve in O(N * 3 * 3) time with O(1) space.
rows.outputFormat: Return the maximum merit points Ninja can achieve.

examples.explanation: Day 1: Activity 2 (70), Day 2: Activity 1 (50), Day 3: Activity 2 (90). Total = 210.

rows.title: Count Square Submatrices with All Ones
rows.description: Given a `m x n` matrix of ones and zeros, return how many square submatrices have all ones. DP relation: if `matrix[i][j] == 1`, `dp[i][j] = 1 + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1], dp[i-1][j-1])`. Summing all `dp[i][j]` yields total square submatrices in O(m * n) time.
rows.outputFormat: Return the total count of square submatrices with all 1s.

examples.explanation: Squares of side 1: 10; squares of side 2: 4; square of side 3: 1. Total = 15.
Squares of side 1: 6; square of side 2: 1. Total = 7.

rows.title: Longest common subsequence
rows.description: Given two strings `text1` and `text2`, return the length of their longest common subsequence. If there is no common subsequence, return 0. A subsequence of a string is a new string generated from the original string with some characters (can be none) deleted without changing the relative order of the remaining characters. Solve in O(M * N) time and O(N) space using 2D DP.
rows.outputFormat: Return the length of the longest common subsequence as an integer.
rows.constraints:
1 <= text1.length, text2.length <= 1000
text1 and text2 consist of only lowercase English characters.

examples.explanation: The longest common subsequence is "ace" and its length is 3.
There is no such common subsequence, so the result is 0.

rows.title: Rotten Oranges
rows.description: You are given an `m x n` grid where each cell can have one of three values: 0 (empty), 1 (fresh orange), 2 (rotten orange). Every minute, any fresh orange that is 4-directionally adjacent to a rotten orange becomes rotten. Return the minimum number of minutes that must elapse until no cell has a fresh orange. If this is impossible, return -1. Solve in O(m * n) using multi-source BFS.
rows.inputFormat: An `m x n` 2D grid containing 0s, 1s, and 2s.
rows.outputFormat: Return minimum minutes, or -1 if fresh oranges remain.
rows.constraints:
m == grid.length
n == grid[i].length
1 <= m, n <= 10
grid[i][j] is 0, 1, or 2.

examples.explanation: In 4 minutes, all fresh oranges rot.
The bottom-left fresh orange cannot be reached.

rows.title: Shortest path in undirected graph with unit weights
rows.description: You are given an undirected graph with `V` vertices and unit edge weights (weight = 1 for all edges). Find the shortest path from a given source vertex `src` to all other vertices. If a vertex is not reachable, distance is -1. Solve in O(V + E) time using standard Breadth-First Search (BFS).
rows.inputFormat: An integer `V`, edge list, and source vertex `src`.
rows.outputFormat: Return an array of distances from `src` to all vertices.

examples.explanation: BFS guarantees shortest path in unit weight graphs.

rows.title: Maximum sum of non adjacent elements
rows.description: Given an array of integers `nums`, find the maximum sum of a subsequence such that no two elements in the subsequence are adjacent in the array. Solve in O(N) time and O(1) space maintaining `pick` and `notPick` states.
rows.outputFormat: Return the maximum non-adjacent sum.

rows.title: Largest Divisible Subset
rows.description: Given a set of distinct positive integers `nums`, return the largest subset `answer` such that every pair `(answer[i], answer[j])` satisfies `answer[i] % answer[j] == 0` or `answer[j] % answer[i] == 0`. Sort the array first and adapt the Longest Increasing Subsequence algorithm using the divisibility condition.
rows.inputFormat: An integer array `nums` of distinct positive integers.
rows.outputFormat: Return a list representing the largest divisible subset.
rows.constraints:
1 <= nums.length <= 1000
1 <= nums[i] <= 2 * 10^9
All elements are unique.

examples.explanation: Every element divides the subsequent one.

rows.title: Number of enclaves
rows.description: You are given an `m x n` binary matrix `grid`, where `0` represents a sea cell and `1` represents a land cell. A move consists of walking from one land cell to another 4-directionally adjacent land cell or walking off the boundary of the grid. Return the number of land cells in `grid` for which we cannot walk off the boundary of the grid in any number of moves. Solve by running BFS/DFS from boundary land cells to mark escapable cells, then counting remaining 1s.
rows.outputFormat: Return the number of enclosed land cells.
rows.constraints:
m == grid.length
n == grid[i].length
1 <= m, n <= 500
grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

examples.explanation: The three 1s in the center cannot reach any boundary.
All 1s are connected to the boundary.

rows.title: Course Schedule I
rows.description: There are a total of `numCourses` courses you have to take, labeled from `0` to `numCourses - 1`. You are given an array `prerequisites` where `prerequisites[i] = [a, b]` indicates that you must take course `b` first if you want to take course `a`. Return `true` if you can finish all courses, or `false` otherwise (equivalent to detecting if the prerequisite dependency graph contains a cycle). Solve in O(V + E) using Kahn's algorithm.
rows.inputFormat: An integer `numCourses` and a list of pairs `prerequisites`.
rows.outputFormat: Return boolean `true` if courses can be completed, else `false`.
rows.constraints:
1 <= numCourses <= 2000
0 <= prerequisites.length <= 5000
prerequisites[i].length == 2
All pairs are unique.

examples.explanation: To take course 1, you must finish course 0. Valid order: [0, 1].

rows.title: Find the city with the smallest number of neighbors
rows.description: There are `n` cities numbered from `0` to `n - 1`. Given an array `edges` where `edges[i] = [from_i, to_i, weight_i]` and an integer `distanceThreshold`, return the city with the smallest number of cities that are reachable through some path and whose distance is at most `distanceThreshold`. If there are multiple such cities, return the city with the greatest number. Solve in O(N^3) using Floyd-Warshall.
rows.outputFormat: Return the city index.

examples.explanation: City 3 has 2 neighbors within threshold 4, and has the greatest index.

rows.title: Introduction to DP

Learn how to optimize space complexity by keeping only the necessary previous states (e.g. `prev` and `prev2` for Fibonacci).
rows.outputFormat: Return the n-th Fibonacci number computed via dynamic programming.

rows.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Cooldown
rows.description: You are given an array `prices` where `prices[i]` is the price of a given stock on the `i`-th day. Find the maximum profit you can achieve. After you sell your stock, you cannot buy stock on the next day (i.e., cooldown one day). Solve in O(N) time and O(1) space with 3 states: `buy`, `sell`, and `cooldown`.
rows.outputFormat: Return maximum profit with cooldown.

rows.title: Number of Longest Increasing Subsequences
rows.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return the number of longest increasing subsequences. Track both `len[i]` (length of LIS ending at i) and `count[i]` (number of LIS of that length ending at i) in O(N^2) time.
rows.outputFormat: Return total count of LIS sequences.

examples.explanation: The two LIS of length 4 are [1, 3, 4, 7] and [1, 3, 5, 7].
Each element forms an LIS of length 1.

rows.title: Course Schedule II
rows.description: There are a total of `numCourses` courses you have to take, labeled from `0` to `numCourses - 1`. Given prerequisites `[a, b]` (take b before a), return the ordering of courses you should take to finish all courses. If there are many valid answers, return any of them. If it is impossible to finish all courses, return an empty array `[]`. Solve using Kahn's Topological Sort in O(V + E) time.
rows.inputFormat: An integer `numCourses` and array of prerequisite pairs.
rows.outputFormat: Return an array representing a valid course completion order, or [].

rows.title: Accounts merge
rows.description: Given a list of `accounts` where each element `accounts[i]` is a list of strings, where the first element `accounts[i][0]` is a name, and the rest of the elements are emails representing that account. Merge these accounts using Disjoint Set Union by mapping each email to a unique account ID and taking union of all emails in the same account.
rows.inputFormat: A list of lists of strings `accounts`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the merged accounts list with sorted emails.

examples.explanation: The first two accounts share "johnsmith@mail.com" and are merged into one.
No common emails, accounts remain separate.

rows.title: Partition a set into two subsets with minimum absolute sum difference
rows.description: Given an integer array `nums`, partition it into two non-empty subsets such that the absolute difference between their sums is minimized. Return the minimum absolute sum difference. Solve in O(N * totalSum) using the last row of the subset-sum DP table.
rows.outputFormat: Return the minimum absolute sum difference.

rows.title: Kosaraju's algorithm
rows.description: Given a Directed Graph with `V` vertices and `E` edges, find the number of Strongly Connected Components (SCCs) in the graph. A Strongly Connected Component is a maximal subgraph where every vertex is reachable from any other vertex in that subgraph. Implement Kosaraju's Algorithm in O(V + E) time: 1. Sort vertices by finish time using DFS. 2. Transpose the graph (reverse all edges). 3. Perform DFS in order of finish times.
rows.inputFormat: An integer `V` and adjacency list `adj` of a directed graph.
rows.outputFormat: Return the number of strongly connected components.

rows.title: Best time to buy and sell stock
rows.description: You are given an array `prices` where `prices[i]` is the price of a given stock on the `i`-th day. You want to maximize your profit by choosing a single day to buy one stock and choosing a different day in the future to sell that stock. Return the maximum profit you can achieve. Solve in O(N) time and O(1) space tracking the minimum price seen so far.
rows.outputFormat: Return the maximum achievable profit.

examples.explanation: Buy on day 2 (price = 1) and sell on day 5 (price = 6), profit = 6 - 1 = 5.
Prices continuously fall, no positive profit achievable.

rows.title: House robber
rows.description: You are a professional robber planning to rob houses along a circular street. Each house has a certain amount of money stashed. Since adjacent houses have security systems connected, you cannot rob two adjacent houses. Furthermore, the first and last house are neighbors! Return the maximum amount of money you can rob tonight without alerting the police. Solve using two passes of Maximum Sum of Non-Adjacent Elements: `max(rob(0..n-2), rob(1..n-1))`.
rows.inputFormat: An integer array `nums` representing cash in each circular house.
rows.outputFormat: Return the maximum stolen cash.

examples.explanation: Cannot rob house 1 (money 2) and house 3 (money 2) because they are adjacent in a circle. Max is 3.

rows.title: Longest Bitonic Subsequence
rows.description: Given an array of positive integers `nums`, find the length of the Longest Bitonic Subsequence. A subsequence is bitonic if it is first strictly increasing, and then strictly decreasing. Solve in O(N^2) time by calculating LIS from left `dp1[]` and LIS from right `dp2[]`, then maximizing `dp1[i] + dp2[i] - 1`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the maximum length of a bitonic subsequence.

rows.title: Bridges in graph
rows.description: An edge in an undirected connected graph is a bridge (critical connection) if removing it disconnects the graph. Given `n` servers numbered from `0` to `n - 1` and a list of server connections, return all critical connections in the network. Solve in O(V + E) time using Tarjan's bridge-finding algorithm tracking discovery time `tin[u]` and lowest reachable time `low[u]` (`low[v] > tin[u]`).
rows.outputFormat: Return a list of bridge edges `[u, v]`.
rows.constraints:
2 <= n <= 10^5
n - 1 <= connections.length <= 10^5
All connections unique.

examples.explanation: Edge [1, 3] is the only bridge because removing it isolates node 3.

rows.title: Partition equal subset sum
rows.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return `true` if you can partition the array into two subsets such that the sum of the elements in both subsets is equal or `false` otherwise. If `totalSum` is odd, return `false`. Otherwise, reduce to finding a subset with sum `totalSum / 2`.
rows.outputFormat: Return boolean `true` if equal partition exists, else `false`.

examples.explanation: The array can be partitioned as [1, 5, 5] and [11].
Total sum is 11 (odd), cannot be partitioned equally.

rows.title: Longest common substring
rows.description: Given two strings `s1` and `s2`, find the length of the longest common substring between them (contiguous characters). If `s1[i-1] == s2[j-1]`, then `dp[i][j] = 1 + dp[i-1][j-1]`; otherwise `dp[i][j] = 0`. Track the global maximum in O(M * N) time and O(N) space.
rows.outputFormat: Return the length of the longest common contiguous substring.
rows.constraints:
1 <= s1.length, s2.length <= 1000
s1 and s2 consist of lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: The longest common substring is "CDGH" with length 4.

rows.title: Making a large island
rows.description: You are given an `n x n` binary matrix `grid`. You are allowed to change at most one `0` to be `1`. Return the size of the largest island in `grid` after applying this operation. Solve in O(N^2) time using Disjoint Set Union: precompute island sizes and check which distinct islands are connected by flipping each zero.
rows.outputFormat: Return the maximum island size.
rows.constraints:
n == grid.length == grid[i].length
1 <= n <= 500
grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

examples.explanation: Change one 0 to 1 to connect the two 1s into an island of size 3.
Grid is already all 1s; island size is 4.

rows.title: Best time to buy and sell stock III
rows.description: Find the maximum profit you can achieve from a stock prices array with at most two transactions. You may not engage in multiple transactions simultaneously. Solve in O(N) time and O(1) space using 4 states: `buy1`, `sell1`, `buy2`, `sell2` or DP `dp[i][buy][cap]`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the maximum profit with at most 2 transactions.

examples.explanation: Buy on day 4 (price 0) and sell on day 6 (price 3), profit = 3. Buy on day 7 (price 1) and sell on day 8 (price 4), profit = 3. Total = 6.
Single transaction buy day 1, sell day 5 gives 4.

rows.title: Print Longest Increasing Subsequence
rows.description: Given an integer array `nums`, find and print the actual elements forming the Longest Increasing Subsequence. Solve in O(N^2) time using an array `parent[]` to backtrack the chosen sequence.
rows.outputFormat: Return the list of integers forming the LIS.

examples.explanation: Length is 6 and the sequence is strictly increasing.

rows.title: Articulation point in graph
rows.description: Given an undirected connected graph with `V` vertices and `E` edges, find all the Articulation Points (cut vertices) in the graph. An articulation point is a vertex whose removal increases the number of connected components. Solve in O(V + E) time using Tarjan's algorithm: a node `u` is an articulation point if `low[v] >= tin[u]` for a child `v` (or if `u` is root with > 1 children).
rows.outputFormat: Return a list of articulation point vertices sorted in ascending order, or [-1].

examples.explanation: Removing vertex 1 or vertex 4 disconnects the graph.

rows.title: Triangle
rows.description: Given a `triangle` array, return the minimum path sum from top to bottom. For each step, you may move to an adjacent number of the row below. More formally, if you are on index `i` on the current row, you may move to either index `i` or index `i + 1` on the next row. Solve in O(N^2) time and O(N) space using bottom-up DP.
rows.inputFormat: A list of lists of integers representing a triangle.
rows.outputFormat: Return the minimum path sum from apex to base.

examples.explanation: The minimum path sum from top to bottom is 2 + 3 + 5 + 1 = 11.

rows.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
rows.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence. Solve in O(N^2) time using dynamic programming, or in O(N log N) time using patience sorting with binary search (`lower_bound`).
rows.outputFormat: Return the length of the longest increasing subsequence.

examples.explanation: The longest increasing subsequence is [2, 3, 7, 101], therefore the length is 4.

rows.title: Number of islands II
rows.description: You are given an `n x m` 2D grid initially filled with water (0). You are given an array `operators` where each operator `[row, col]` turns water into land (1). After each operation, find the number of islands. Solve online using Disjoint Set Union with 4-directional neighbor connections in O(k * alpha(n * m)) time.
rows.inputFormat: Integers `n`, `m`, and a 2D array of positions `operators`.
rows.outputFormat: Return an array of integers showing island count after each operation.

examples.explanation: Island counts updated dynamically as lands connect.

rows.title: Count partitions with given difference
rows.description: Given an array `nums` of `n` integers and an integer `d`. Find the number of ways to partition the array into two subsets `S1` and `S2` such that `sum(S1) >= sum(S2)` and `sum(S1) - sum(S2) = d`. Formula: `sum(S1) = (totalSum + d) / 2`. If `(totalSum + d)` is odd or `totalSum < d`, return 0.
rows.inputFormat: An integer array `nums` and integer difference `d`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the number of partitions modulo 10^9 + 7.

examples.explanation: Six ways to partition into two equal subsets of sum 2.

rows.title: Best time to buy and sell stock IV
rows.description: You are given an integer array `prices` where `prices[i]` is the price of a given stock on the `i`-th day, and an integer `k`. Find the maximum profit you can achieve. You may complete at most `k` transactions. Solve in O(N * K) time and O(K) space using DP.
rows.inputFormat: An integer `k` and an integer array `prices`.
rows.outputFormat: Return the maximum profit with at most `k` transactions.

examples.explanation: Buy on day 1 (price 2) and sell on day 2 (price 4), profit = 2.
Buy day 2 sell day 3 (profit 4); buy day 5 sell day 6 (profit 3). Total = 7.

rows.title: Longest String Chain
rows.description: You are given an array of `words` where each word consists of lowercase English letters. `wordA` is a predecessor of `wordB` if and only if we can insert exactly one letter anywhere in `wordA` without changing the order of the other characters to make it equal to `wordB`. Return the length of the longest possible word chain with words chosen from the given list of words.
rows.outputFormat: Return the integer length of the longest word chain.
rows.constraints:
1 <= words.length <= 1000
1 <= words[i].length <= 16
words[i] only consists of lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: One of the longest word chains is ["a", "ba", "bda", "bdca"].

rows.title: Minimum coins
rows.description: You are given an integer array `coins` representing coins of different denominations and an integer `amount` representing a total amount of money. Return the fewest number of coins that you need to make up that amount. If that amount of money cannot be made up by any combination of the coins, return -1. You may assume that you have an infinite number of each kind of coin. Solve in O(N * amount) using unbounded knapsack DP.
rows.outputFormat: Return the minimum coin count, or -1.
